title: fix(2d): start-side Arc entry plunges in air outside the stock box
body:
## What changed

A 2D Offset pass that starts Inside or Outside round a part now enters by the Arc entry from the air outside the stock box (new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/air_entry.rs`).

1. The tool plunges in air at a point P. The distance from P to the stock box is at least the tool radius plus `approach_distance` (#3745).
2. In the cut plane, a straight lead in air (tangent to the arc), then one G17 arc of Arc radius and Arc sweep, tangent to the first cut at the pass start. A change of Arc radius or Arc sweep changes the arc in the output.
3. The lead is proved with the proof of the horizontal arc entry (`descent_xy::arc_at`, made `pub(super)`) against the cutter-centre area joined with the air outside the box, and across none of the planned passes. Thus it touches no part and crosses no ring.
4. When no air lead fits, the entry stands down to a named helix, then a named ramp along the first cut, else the op is refused by name (`AIR_ENTRY_REFUSAL`, read by `approach::refusal`). The axial dive and the vertical arc ramp into material are no longer stand-ins.
5. A re-entry after a lift onto a start in material (`entry_restart`) tries the air entry first. On a start-side pass it then tries a clear helix before the named plunge.

Inside: the other rings enclose the first Inside ring, so each lead from the air crosses rings at the cut Z. The verifier's Crossing law holds such a post. Thus Inside takes the named helix (or ramp), never a plunge into material. The decision and the dropped options are in `docs/decisions/3746-air-entry.md`.

The pass links (`level_link`, `pass_link`, `link_proof`) are not changed (#3747 owns them).

## Readings (dog bone, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, Arc entry)

- Before: Outside plunged at (39.400, -24.400), 0.000 mm off the stock box, note "the arc's lead room is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead". Inside entered with the vertical arc, whose first chords are a plunge into material by `plunge_law::first_solid_plunge`.
- After: Outside plunges 6 mm or more off the box (R 4 + approach 2); the first cut is a G17 arc of radius 8 (Arc radius 0) and a quarter turn (Arc sweep 0); radius 6 / 10 and sweep 60 show in the output. Inside: no plunge into material; the entry is named.
- fig8 Outside, Arc entry: each level is entered from the air with a first arc. Four re-entries after a pass-link lift still plunge into material, named (no air lead, helix or ramp reaches their starts clear of the cut rings).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `machining2d::air_entry::tests`: `outside_entry_plunges_in_air`, `outside_first_cut_is_an_arc_in_the_plane`, `arc_radius_changes_the_lead`, `inside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`, `outside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`. All five were red with the air room off (the `main` behaviour) and are green now.
- `camcraft-app` `offset_pass_start` (heavy): `fig8_start_sides_enter_from_the_air` (green).
- `fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material`: known-fail #3747 (the four re-entry plunges come from pass-link lifts).

## Gates

- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6): 171 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: offset_pass_start"`: ok (5 passed, including the existing fig8 Outside, Inside and crossing pins).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The avoid route (`pocket_avoid_started_on`, fixtures and clamps) keeps its old entry. The air outside the box is not proved free of fixtures there. Follow-up: #3810.
- A user-selected Helix, Ramp or Plunge keeps its entry; its warning and the Arc default are #3748.
- The Lead in / Lead out page already offers all four kinds for each start side and greys none out (`lead_page.rs`). No UI change.
- The light lane was not run.
- `descent.rs` was 411 lines and is 418 now (the new `Descent::Air` arms).

Changelog: 2D Offset "Pass starts at" Inside and Outside: the Arc entry plunges in air outside the stock box (tool radius plus the approach distance) and arcs onto the first ring in the cut plane with the Arc radius and Arc sweep; where no air entry fits, a named helix or ramp is used, never a plunge into material.

Effort: max

Fixes #3746

title: fix(motion): 2D Offset rings link in the plane, lift only with a named reason
body:
## What changed

Round a part (2D Offset "Pass starts at" Inside, Outside, and Auto when it resolves), the rings stay at depth and the links stay in the cut plane. A lift occurs only when each in-plane link fails, and a `link:` note names the reason.

- `level_order::linkable` (the join law of the plan) accepts a chord through air as well as through cut material. A centre is in air when it is 0.1 tool radii or more outside the stock footprint.
- When the straight chord fails, the plan tries an edge route (`ring_links::edge_route`). The route goes to the edge of the cutter-centre area, along that edge, and back to the next piece. Each chord of the route obeys the same join law. The route goes through each walk vertex on the edge, so a piece that ends there is touched at a shared vertex and not crossed.
- `ladder_links::pass_link` of a ring area uses the ring law (`ring_links::link`) for all pass link values. The straight link is fed when it is proved. Else the tool lifts to the retract plane, and the tally names the reason: the stay-down limit, the part, a fixture ("Do not touch"), a crossing, or uncut stock.
- A pocket (`around_part: false`) keeps its links byte for byte (#3752 owns it). The entry, the level link and the re-entry after a lift do not change (#3746 owns the entry).
- No `Links::RINGS` seed: the law is in the motion layer, so an old project file gets the same path. #3750 owns the seed. See `docs/decisions/3747-in-plane-ring-links.md`.

## Readings

`pass_start_levels::ring_links`: 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, one level.

| Case | Before (lifts, no reason) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Disc, Inside | 20 | 0 |
| Disc, Outside / Auto | - | 0 |
| Dog bone, Inside | 15 | 0 |
| Dog bone, Outside | - | 0 |
| Clamp across the band, Inside / Outside | - | 3 / 26, each named ("fixture") |

fig8 (heavy, release): Inside 6 lifts in a level, 6 named. Outside 12 lifts, 12 named. Each lift that is left has a named reason.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels`: `ring_links::start_side_rings_do_not_lift`, `ring_links::dogbone_start_side_lifts`, `ring_links::lift_reason_is_named` (red first: 20 and 15 lifts, 0 named). The pins also assert no overcut (shape mask, the gouge check) and no crossing feeds (`verify::crossed_pairs`). The clamp pin asserts `avoid_hits` is empty.
- `camcraft-app` `offset_pass_start`: `lifts::fig8_start_sides_lift_only_with_a_named_reason` (heavy).

## Gates

- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6): 171 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Targeted heavy step `app heavy: offset_pass_start` (release, `--ignored`): 5 passed, 0 failed. This includes `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing`, `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` and the new pin.

## Not exercised

- No full heavy lanes and no light lane.
- The private model of #3741 was not run.
- 2D Pocket Inside and Outside do not change (#3752).
- `levels.rs` grows from 457 to 460 lines (one field), and `offset_pass_start.rs` from 418 to 419 lines (one `mod` line). The new code is in `ring_links.rs` (322 lines).

#3423 (lifts between pieces) is covered by this change. Close it when this PR merges.

Changelog: 2D Offset "Pass starts at" Inside, Outside and Auto: the rings stay at depth and link in the cut plane (through air or cut material, and along the edge of the area); the tool lifts only where each in-plane link would cut the part, hit a fixture or cross a cut, and a note names the reason.

Effort: max

Fixes #3747

title: fix(sim): check bull-nose gouges in the finish envelope
body:
## Change

Use the specified bull-nose corner radius to check straight, upright cuts for a gouge in the native Envelope verifier. The check reports remaining stock as unmeasured.

## Evidence

- The original native verifier missed the two R1 gouges. The patched verifier reports both. The tangent R1 rail and the R3 control remain free of gouges.
- The independent oracle measured 0.100 mm of gouge for the lowered Ø8 R1 rail. The same-diameter ball had 0.193 mm of clearance.
- The oracle measured 0.633 mm of vertical rest at the R3 test point. The native R3 result reports `RestUnjudged`.
- The explicit and implicit ball profiles produce identical warnings on the same rail. The existing numeric ball-envelope test also passes.

## Verification

- Windows native quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) passed all six steps on `f48a9aaf6`. It ran 270 tests with zero failures or skips.
- The native baseline ran the same three regression cases. All three failed as expected, and the ten existing tests passed.
- The independent rail oracle passed all seven checks.

## Pinning tests

- `bullnose_envelope::bullnose_envelope_catches_the_r1_gouge_that_the_ball_misses`
- `bullnose_envelope::bullnose_envelope_distinguishes_r1_from_r3_on_the_same_rail`
- `bullnose_envelope::bullnose_envelope_marks_the_r3_rail_rest_as_unmeasured`

## Scope

The tests use synthetic parts and fixed upright axes. Bull-nose rest measurement, arc and tilted motion, and physical machining were outside this verification.

The issue branch starts at upstream commit `29bb9e9a2`, after cut `v0.26.0`.

Changelog: The Envelope verifier detects gouges from straight, upright bull-nose cuts and reports remaining stock as unmeasured.

Refs #1531

title: fix(2d): name narrow stock bands in generation refusals
body:
## What changed

Name the stock band around the part when a stock-source pocket-family operation refuses because the cutter cannot fit.
The reported reproduction now names the 2.000 mm minimum side width and the 3.000 mm tool.
The refusal also names stock to leave per wall and suggests a smaller tool, wider stock, or a 2D Contour.
True pockets keep their existing refusal, with a part selection and with the stock as the source.
Curved bands receive advice without an invented width.
Generation still refuses the same job and emits no path.

The band message applies only when the area surrounds kept material.
A piece of the stock-minus-part region is a band when its outer loop is a loop of the stock outline, and material stands inside that loop.
A closed pocket and a pocket around an island have part walls as their boundary. They keep the pocket refusal.
A strip of stock beside a part that is flush with the other stock sides also keeps the pocket refusal.

## Cause

The generator reports a generic pocket error before the successful-path band note can run.
The app holds the stock-source context needed to explain that error.

## Tests

Final head: `0d316a6dc57c22d007e08e89c13828e1b5643156`.
Gate base: current `upstream/main` at `cd0222d9cceb5e6f831a13071b93f1d083c3f10e`.

`cargo test -p camcraft-app --test narrow_band` passed all ten tests.
The eight tests of this PR are:

- `a_stock_source_adaptive_refusal_names_the_band_width_and_a_fix`
- `a_stock_band_refusal_names_stock_to_leave`
- `a_stock_band_refusal_measures_the_controlled_boundary`
- `a_part_source_narrow_pocket_keeps_its_own_refusal`
- `a_stock_source_closed_pocket_keeps_its_own_refusal` (review round 1)
- `a_stock_source_pocket_around_an_island_keeps_its_own_refusal` (review round 1)
- `a_stock_band_refusal_uses_document_inches`
- `a_curved_stock_band_refusal_does_not_invent_a_rectangular_width`

Pin proof, first round: the primary pin failed on unchanged upstream code before the fix.
Restoring upstream's exact `run_job.rs` made all five diagnostic pins fail.

Pin proof, review round 1:

- Mutation A disabled the `surrounds_kept_material` guard. The two new controls failed. The other eight tests passed.
- Mutation B kept the guard and disabled only its stock-outline test. `a_stock_source_pocket_around_an_island_keeps_its_own_refusal` failed. The other nine tests passed.
- The restored fix passed all ten tests.

Results on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 148 steps passed, zero failed, zero stalled, 15.5 minutes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 62 steps passed, zero failed, zero stalled, 20.9 minutes.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --only "app suites: example_catalog"`: one step passed, zero failed.

Effort: medium.
No escalation.

## Goldens moved

None.
The catalog suite ran and passed on the final head before this result was recorded.
The quick gate's `adaptive_trochoid` posted-program golden checks also passed.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- '*.nc' '*.cl' examples/catalog` produced no changes.

## Not exercised

No GUI or physical controller run.
The diagnostic does not infer numeric widths for arbitrary band shapes.
No test covers a tilted (3+2) stock-source band. The guard reads the stock facets in the frame of the region there.
No test covers the strip beside a flush part. It has no hole, so the guard keeps the pocket refusal.

## Overlaps

None found in the three Step 2 file checks.
The branch starts at `upstream/main` commit `3c68dcaf2` and is not stacked.
The branch merges cleanly with the current `upstream/main`.

Changelog: Explain narrow stock-band refusals with the band width, tool size, stock to leave, and corrective advice.

Fixes #3791

title: build(kernel): bump solidcore to the synced fork rev fa67b3f5
body:
## What changed

- **Fork sync.** The fork `NeoTech/solidcore` `main` was 0 commits ahead and 300 commits behind `tangency-labs/solidcore` `main`. It took the 300 upstream commits by a fast-forward (GitHub merge-upstream). There was no force-push. The fork is now equal to upstream at `fa67b3f560b7a8d59e99cb728f72f85e91dee2da` (2026-11-23). The old pin was `2016386442dfee3b2a0c3a1bfdd4017c5254dac8` (2026-11-19).
- **Pin.** `crates/kernel/Cargo.toml` pins the six solidcore crates at the full new rev.
- **Cargo.lock.** Only the six solidcore packages change (`solidcore`, `-step`, `-convert`, `-ops`, `-record`, `-tess`).
- **#3742.** The unused workspace line `truck-polymesh = "=0.6.0"` is removed. The build does not print the warning now. `truck-polymesh` stays in `Cargo.lock` as a dependency of `truck-meshalgo`.
- **LICENSES.md.** The solidcore section names the new rev. The NOTICE and LICENSE blobs at `fa67b3f5` are the same as at `55d0e763`.
- **One code change** in `camcraft_geometry::step_diag::record_parses` (see "Readings").

## Dependencies and licences

| Package | Change | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| solidcore, solidcore-step, solidcore-convert, solidcore-ops, solidcore-record, solidcore-tess | rev `2016386` -> `fa67b3f5` | Apache-2.0 (workspace licence, unchanged) |
| serde 1.0.229 | `solidcore-ops` uses it as a dependency now (it was a dev-dependency). The package was already in the lock. | MIT OR Apache-2.0 |

No new package is in `Cargo.lock`. Thus `needs-maintainer` is not set.

## Readings: the pins that moved, and why

Each file is still refused or still measured exactly. No assert was widened.

1. `twisted_flank_off.step` (kernel `step_agreement` row, kernel, geometry and app `step_twisted_flank`). Still refused as `#117`. The reader now builds the pcurves, and the vertex check refuses the solid: `#117 at check: a vertex sits 3.430e-1 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3)`. It was `#117 at read: pcurves failed on ...`. The new message does not name face #93, so the app pin drops that one assert.
2. `edge_gap_021_stated_5mm.step` (kernel and geometry `step_edge_gap`). It was kept by the reader and refused by the machining mesh at the chord. Now the kernel gap check refuses it at the read, and names the 0.02 mm cap and the stated 5 mm. This is an earlier refusal of the same file.
3. `cube-chamfer-all-12-d2` (kernel `blend`). The volume moves from 802.667 to 808.000 mm3. Upstream "retire the fillet_chamfer_corner flag (chamfer-corner event is the only chamfer corner) (#21269)" makes three equal chamfers meet in one mitred vertex, with no flat bevel triangle. The closed form drops the d^3/12 tetrahedron for each corner. It agrees with the new solid exactly (|dV| < 1e-9).
4. `provoke_face_left_out_edge_not_sampled_and_lenient` case 3 (kernel `machining_mesh_shortfalls`). The self-crossing inner loop now gives `NotWatertight { open: 6 }`, not `Lenient`. It is still a refusal. No test reaches the `Lenient` arm now: follow-up #3800.
5. `step_nesting::a_record_at_the_cap_still_imports` and `parentheses_inside_text_are_not_counted` (app). The new Part 21 parser holds the counts of a text to the density of its own length (one parameter for each 4 bytes). `step_diag` probes each DATA record alone in a short frame. Thus a dense legal record was refused as a syntax error, and the import failed. The probe now reads `TooManyParams`, `TooManyRecords` and `TooManyEntities` as "no syntax fault". The parse of the whole file still applies the limits. New pin: `step_diag::a_dense_legal_record_is_not_named` (red without the fix, green with it).

No toolpath pin moved.

## Tests run (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6, -j 6, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR)

- `camcraft-kernel`: the full debug suite, green (`step_agreement` 29/29, `step_edge_gap`, `step_twisted_flank`, `blend`, `machining_mesh*`, `step_import`, `import_corpus`, `corrupt_input`, `solidcraft_*`, `agreement`, lib).
- `camcraft-geometry`: the full debug suite, green, with `step_diag::a_dense_legal_record_is_not_named`.
- `camcraft-app`, targeted: `import`, `import_step_*` (13 binaries), `step_nesting`, `adaptive_fig8_crossing`, `lead_approach`, `adaptive_pass_start`, `flute_reach`, `feature_edge_g1_join`, `shoulder_adaptive`. All green.
- Targeted heavy step (release, `--ignored`): `adaptive_fig8_crossing::adaptive2d_on_fig8_model_in_tight_stock_has_no_crossings_and_posts` and `adaptive2d_on_fig8_stock_excluding_top_face_has_no_crossings_and_posts`: pass.
- #2849 known-fail `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (release): still fails at the `// known-fail-assert` line with `EM-0800-4FL ends at selected face (dist 31.406, r 4)`. The new solidcore does not fix it. The marker stays valid.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -D warnings` and clippy on `camcraft-app --test import_step_twisted_flank`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The full quick plan (1193 steps: the lock change reaches each crate). The UI suites and the other app binaries did not run.
- The full heavy lanes and the light lane. They run at the cut.
- Linux and macOS builds. The change adds no platform code.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3767-solidcore-bump.md`.

Changelog: STEP import uses solidcore at the newest upstream commit (fa67b3f5). A dense but legal STEP record is no longer refused as a syntax error. The kernel builds three equal chamfers at one corner as one mitred vertex.

Effort: high

Fixes #3742
Fixes #3767

title: fix(post): return the rotary axes to zero at program end (Fanuc, Doosan DNM)
body:
## What changed

- The Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts end a program upright.
- If a rotary is off zero after the last section, the program end writes these blocks before M30:
  - `G49`
  - `G91 G28 Z0` (or `G53 G00 Z<safe_retract>` with `safeRetract` G53)
  - `G90` (G28 mode only)
  - `G00 A0. B0.` (only the rotaries off zero; no X/Y/Z word)
  - `G91 G28 X0 Y0` (G28 mode only)
- Doosan writes `M11` before and `M10` after the return when A turns.
- These are the same blocks as the section return of #3466 (PR #3478).
- A trailing "Go home" ask already lifts Z. Then the end writes only the zero angle block.
- An upright program ends byte for byte as before.
- `heldRotaries()` and `rotariesToZero()` are now shared by the section return and the program end. The section return output does not change.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3540-program-end-rotary-return.md`.

## Cause

The angle words are modal. `onClose()` wrote only the Z and X/Y reference return. The table or the head stayed at the last tilt after M30. On Doosan, G43.4 was also still active at the reference return.

## Tests

Pins (new, in the `upright_after_tilt` suite as the submodule `upright_after_tilt/program_end.rs`; no new test binary):

- `program_end::fanuc_returns_rotaries_before_program_end` (G28 and G53 modes)
- `program_end::doosan_returns_rotaries_before_program_end` (G28 and G53 modes)
- `program_end::doosan_unclamps_and_clamps_a_at_program_end`
- `program_end::upright_program_end_adds_no_rotary_return` (control: the upright end is unchanged)

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged posts, the three return pins failed with "the program commands B0 before M30". The upright control passed.

Mutation results (each restored after the run):

- `fanuc.cps` from upstream/main: the Fanuc pin is red.
- `doosan-dnm.cps` from upstream/main: both Doosan pins are red.
- No `G49` in the Fanuc end: red ("G49 cancels TCPM before the retract").
- `G28 X0 Y0` without `G91` in the Doosan end: red ("the X/Y home is incremental").
- No M11/M10 around the Doosan return: red ("M11 before the A return").
- After each restore: green.

Expected-change updates (each test lists every angle or move word, and the program end adds the return):

- `crates/app/tests/program_units.rs` `rotary_angle_words_are_degrees_in_an_inch_program`: adds `A0.`, `B0.` (tilthead) and `A0.` (Doosan 4th axis).
- `crates/post/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs` `doosan_dnm_index_names_only_a_stated_rotary`: adds `M11`, `G00 A0.`, `M10`.

Commands and results on the final head (54878770e, merged with upstream/main db3bb1f7f):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 145 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 8 steps (release build, `do_not_touch`, `do_not_touch_adaptive`, `example_catalog`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `mcp`, `probe_no_coolant`, `sinker_burn`), 0 failed. The heavy run and the light run were on the head before the merge of upstream/main. That merge brought only `rotary_verify.rs` and two decision files. `rotary_verify` passes on the merged head.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.

## Goldens moved

- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: regenerated with `cargo xtask catalog --case multiaxis/indexed`. Only the end blocks change:

```
 M9
 M5
+G49
 G91 G28 Z0
-G28 X0 Y0
+G90
+G00 A0. B0.
+G91 G28 X0 Y0
 M30
```

- The catalog tool also changed the `version` field of `indexed.camproj`. That change is not related, and it is not in this PR.
- No other `*.nc` or `*.cl` file changed. The example catalog suites pass.

## Not exercised

- No program ran on a real Fanuc or Doosan control.
- The Go-home path at the program end (a trailing `AfterOperation home` on a tilted last section) is not pinned. In that path the end writes only `G00` with the zero angles after the existing home.
- Other rotary posts are not changed:
  - Tormach keeps its final tilt by the decision of #1594.
  - Mach4 also keeps its final pose. It is not in the scope of this issue.
  - Haas and Sinumerik refuse tilted output.

## Overlaps

title: fix(ui): add AI Chat key setup and provider readiness
body:
## What changed

AI Chat can save, replace, remove, and test a provider API key.
It uses the existing OS keychain entries and environment-first lookup.
The entry field clears after save, cancel, and provider changes.
The panel never draws a stored key.

The panel checks cloud readiness when the provider or offline setting changes.
Editing a cloud Model does not read the keychain again.
Ollama Model edits wait for a 500 ms pause before one readiness check.
A cloud Model edit after a finished Test replaces the Test result with "Model changed. Click Test to test this model."
The settings code reads `camcraft_app::clock::Instant`, because the std clock panics in the browser build.
The status names a missing key, an unavailable Ollama server, or a missing model.
Ready means that a key was found. It does not prove that the provider accepted it.
Test sends a small request to the selected model. The provider can bill this request.
Credential and network work runs in the background.

The setup help and guide explain keys, billing, OS permission prompts, and Ollama setup.
They include `ollama serve`, server check commands, `OLLAMA_HOST`, `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`, and `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE`.
They state that a Gemini app subscription does not include an API key.
The help states the current endpoint limit.
Remove deletes the stored key only. It does not revoke a key or remove an environment variable.

Effort: medium

This PR supplies part of #3781. It does not close that issue.

title: ci(release): package the Arch build from the Linux release binaries
body:
## What changed

- `.github/workflows/aur-package.yml` compiles nothing now. It downloads the `linux-packages` artifact of the same run. It unpacks `camcraft-ui`, `camcraft-cli` and `post` from `camcraft-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`.
- `makepkg -o --noprepare -d` gets, checks and extracts the recipe source. Then `makepkg -R -d` runs only `package()` around the prebuilt binaries.
- A CI copy of the recipe (`PKGBUILD.prebuilt`, not committed) adds `'!strip' '!debug'`. makepkg then does not change the binaries.
- A new check compares the SHA256 of each packaged binary with the binary in the Linux tarball. A difference fails the job. On a tag run, the tarball version must agree with the tag.
- A dispatch run packages the assets of its own checkout, because its binaries come from that checkout.
- The job installs only `base-devel` and `curl`. It installs no Rust and no library headers.
- `aur/PKGBUILD` and `aur/.SRCINFO` do not change. They stay the from-source recipe for AUR users. The `.SRCINFO` check still runs.
- `release.yml`: one comment line on the `aur` job. No trigger and no `on:` block changed.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3773-aur-reuse-linux.md`.

## Readings

- Tag run 45269109413 (v0.25.0): `aur / build` ran 21:42:18 -> 22:31:11, that is 48 min 53 s, about 49 billed Linux minutes.
- `publish` waited for the AUR job for 30 minutes after the last other platform (macOS ended at 22:01:16).
- Expected after: about 2-4 minutes (container pull, `pacman -Syu base-devel curl`, artifact download, `makepkg -R`). Expected saving: about 45 billed minutes for each tag run. The release page goes out about 30 minutes earlier.

## How tested

- Both workflow files parse as YAML (`yaml.safe_load`).
- Each `run:` script of the AUR job passes `bash -n`.
- The `options=` sed edit was run on `aur/PKGBUILD`. It gives `options=('!lto' '!strip' '!debug')`, and the guard `grep` matches.

## Not exercised

- The job did not run. A `workflow_dispatch` of `release.yml` without `site_only` builds all platforms, which is a full release run. `site_only` skips `linux` and thus `aur`. No Docker is on this machine for a local Arch container run.
- The first real run is the next tag run, or a dispatch that the maintainer starts.

This is a `.github` change. It waits for the maintainer's read (`needs-maintainer`).

title: fix(2d): one contour-parallel ring set for Pass starts at Auto, Inside and Outside
body:
## What changed

An area round a part (`StartSide::around_part`, the 2D Offset Outside band) now has one ring set for each start side. The rings are the offsets of the part, clipped to the cutter-centre area. Decision: `docs/decisions/3744-one-ring-set.md`.

- Inside walks the set from the part out (the old Inside order).
- Outside walks the same pieces mirrored (`ring_side::mirror`). Each piece runs the other way, so climb stays climb. The outer edge is the first ring and the part wall is the last ring.
- Auto selects one side in one place (`ring_side::resolve`). Auto is Outside when the stock footprint is known and the outer edge stays in air, else Inside. The resolved side drives the rings, the links and the entry. `generate.rs` sends the stock footprint for Auto round a part.
- Round a part, the #3567 dead-end ramp marks stop (issue step 6). Pockets keep them; #3748 retires them.
- `ring_side::share_ends` snaps a ring end onto the boundary walk within 0.1 um, the closing chord included. A ring end 3 nm off its chord gave a crossing on the block of `shoulder_adaptive`.
- #3788 (c): `order()` judges a full-width cut by the flanks law of the meter (`level_flanks`). Each full-width cut is named on the path.
- #3788 (a): fill rings (`ring_fill`). Where the rings of two sides of the part merge, a band gets the same distance curve at half (and a quarter) of a step. A fill is a level curve of the same distance, so it crosses no ring, and Inside and Outside walk the same fills.
- Not changed: pockets, the 3-D levels (their levels are only renumbered), the Adaptive plan, the entry (#3746) and the links (#3747).

## Readings

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Dog bone: Outside floor runs that end on the part wall (the last run excluded) | 13 of 14 | 0 |
| Dog bone: Inside and Outside ring sets | 30 and 22 pieces, different | equal |
| Auto | `waterline_passes` | the path of Outside (stock known) or Inside (no stock) |
| fig8 Outside: full-width meter points | 0 (stock-parallel rings); 495 (one set, without fills) | 21 (single samples at 7 ring corners on 3 levels), named |
| fig8 Inside: full-width meter points | 10686, waist cuts not named | 10662, each named (wall note and narrow note) |
| fig8 crossings, Inside and Outside | not read | 0 |

## Pins

- `machining2d::ring_side::tests::inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings` (red first)
- `machining2d::ring_side::tests::auto_picks_one_side_of_the_one_ring_set` (red first)
- `machining2d::ring_side::tests::the_mirror_reverses_each_piece_and_swaps_the_ends_of_the_order`
- `machining2d::ring_side::tests::a_ring_end_off_the_boundary_chord_by_nanometres_is_shared`
- `machining2d::level_flanks::tests::the_flanks_law_reads_a_slot_and_passes_a_side_cut`
- `machining2d::ring_fill::tests::a_band_with_a_ring_gap_gets_a_fill_and_a_whole_band_none`
- `pass_start_levels::one_ring_set::outside_rings_follow_the_part` (red first: 14 of 14)
- `pass_start_levels::one_ring_set::auto_is_inside_or_outside` (red first)
- `pass_start_levels::one_ring_set::the_one_ring_set_posts_no_crossing_feeds`
- `offset_pass_start::fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing` (heavy; not shown red first)
- `offset_pass_start::fig8_inside_offset_names_each_full_width_cut` (heavy)

## Pins whose reading moved

- `offset_pass_start::fig8_auto_offset_keeps_every_lateral_rapid_at_the_clearance_plane`: Auto is Outside on fig8, so each level starts outside the stock box. The issue asks for this.
- `offset_pass_start::fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (heavy): 0 -> at most 21 points, each named by the narrow note, and no wall note. The 21 are single samples at 7 ring corners. #3788 stays open for them. The pin goes back to 0 when they are fixed.

## Gates (head `6be6b1265`)

- `camcraft-motion --lib` (machining2d, machining3d): 294 passed.
- `camcraft-motion`: `pass_start_levels`, `pass_start_engagement`, `pocket3d_pass_start`, `avoid_adaptive`, `top_z_stock_over`, `circular_ring_links`, `bore_pass_start`, `finish3d_pass_start`: green.
- `camcraft-app` (debug): `offset_pass_start`, `pocket_pass_start`, `pocket3d_pass_start`, `adaptive_pass_start`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `flute_reach`, `strategy_fallback`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Targeted heavy step `app heavy: offset_pass_start`: 4 passed.
- The full quick gate ran green on `ef3372b11`, the head before the review. It did not run again on this head.

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate on this head, the other heavy lanes, and the light lane.
- The private model of #3741.

Changelog: 2D Offset "Pass starts at" round a part: Auto, Inside and Outside now cut the same contour-parallel rings (offsets of the part), with fill rings where two sides of the part merge. The choice changes only the start side and the ring order, and Auto selects Inside or Outside. Outside rings no longer stop on the part wall, and each cut of the full tool width is named on the path.

title: fix(post): keep decimal points in Fanuc-family feed words
body:
## What changed

Keep decimal points in Fanuc, Doosan DNM and Mazak feed words.
Keep them on the separate capped rotary feeds in Fanuc and Doosan DNM.
Keep the existing conversion, precision, rounding and rate limits.

Record the manual audit for all 17 posts in [the decision record](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/9c3d2888e36611daea6f02720cf79d3c440350bf/docs/decisions/3690-feed-decimals.md).
Update exact test expectations and regenerate the affected NC programs.

## Cause

The formatters removed the decimal point from whole feeds.
A request for 2 inch/min became F2.
The cited controls can read that unpointed word as 0.02 inch/min.
An explicit point makes the unit clear.

## Tests

Committed head: 9c3d2888e36611daea6f02720cf79d3c440350bf.
Full verification started from upstream main 7868d378680b325246b0dcdcdbf76c421f801cd9.
The checks cover the committed source and NC programs.
The decision record was added after verification.

Pin command: `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test control_feed_decimal_point -- --nocapture`.

title: fix(sim): name rapid contact with the part
body:
## What changed

The part-solid law reports `RapidInPart` when the tool meets the part on a rapid move.
The message names the move.
The stock law keeps its message.
Both findings block the post.
MCP reports `rapid_in_part`.
The UI keeps part and stock findings in separate groups with their move locations.

## Cause

The part-solid law used `RapidInStock` for contact with the part.

## Screenshots

title: fix(post): keep exact G84 tap feed in six mill posts
body:
## What changed

- Six mill posts write the G84 F word with the exact tap feed: `fanuc`, `doosan-dnm`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `tormach`, `linuxcnc`.
- The F word has three decimals in mm/min and four decimals in in/min. Trailing zeros are removed.
- The Fanuc-family posts (`fanuc`, `doosan-dnm`, `mazak`) keep the point on a whole tap feed (`F750.`). This follows their own length-word rule (#1836). `sinumerik`, `tormach` and `linuxcnc` write `F750`.
- Each post checks the pitch that the control reads (written F / written S) against the stream pitch (feed / rpm). A difference of more than 0.01 percent refuses the tap by name, with the operation name. No G84 is written then.
- The F words of other moves do not change. #3690 owns those.
- The approach and the tolerance are the same as the Mach4 fix (#3701, PR #3731).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3699-tap-feed-precision.md`.

## Cause

Each post wrote the G84 feed with `ff()`, which rounds a mm feed to a whole number (`Math.round`) and an inch feed to two decimals. The stream keeps the tap feed at 0.001 mm/min. M1.4 x 0.3 at S115 needs F34.5. The posts wrote `F35`, and the control cut a pitch that is 1.45 percent too long.

## Tests

- New pin: `crates/post/tests/tap_feed_mill_posts.rs`, one test for each post:
  - `fanuc_g84_keeps_exact_tap_feed`
  - `doosan_dnm_g84_keeps_exact_tap_feed`
  - `mazak_g84_keeps_exact_tap_feed`
  - `sinumerik_g84_keeps_exact_tap_feed`
  - `tormach_g84_keeps_exact_tap_feed`
  - `linuxcnc_g84_keeps_exact_tap_feed` (floating tap, which is G84 on LinuxCNC)
- Each test pins: F34.5 at S115 and F133.2 at S333 (the two feeds of the issue), F34.561 (three decimals), a whole feed (`F600.` or `F600`), inch F1.3583 and F5.2441, a refusal for S115.4 (the S word changes the pitch), and a refusal for an inch feed below the smallest step.
- Red before the fix: all 6 tests failed on upstream/main fe385c642 (`left: Some("F35")`, `right: Some("F34.5")`).
- Mutation 1: I removed only the `tapPitchHolds` call in all six posts. All 6 tests failed at the refusal assert. Restored: green.
- Mutation 2: I put back only `fw(p.FeedRate)` for the G84 word in all six posts. All 6 tests failed (`F35`). Restored: green.
- `mach4` already has a three-decimal pin (`F34.561` in `mach4_feed_decimals.rs`, PR #3731). This PR does not change it.
- New top-level test file: `crates/post/tests/` has no directory test suite (its directories are support modules only). The binary is small and runs in milliseconds.

## Gate (on upstream/main fe385c642)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 796 steps, 2 failed. Both failures came from this change, and I fixed them:
  - `fanuc_rigid_tap_m29_without_spindle_speed_is_refused_by_name`: the new pitch check ran before the M29 refusal. The M29 refusal now runs first.
  - `tormach_explains_every_conformance_golden_without_changing_the_program`: the explain golden had the old inch tap feed. I regenerated it (see Goldens moved).
- After the two fixes, on the final head:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all 140 binaries): green.
  - `app suites: conformance`: 7 passed.

title: fix(verify): list plasma law warnings as findings and op warnings
body:
## What changed

- `posting_plasma.rs`: the plasma clause keeps each warning of the laws as data. The new type is `posting::GateWarning { op, kind, message }`. The kinds are `plasma_tip_up` and `plasma_kerf_crossing`. A refusal stays a gate problem.
- `posting.rs`: `GateReport` has a new `warnings` field. `verification_report_by` fills it from the plasma clause.
- `script/api.rs` (`v_verify`): each gate warning goes into the `warnings` row of its operation. It also goes into a new `gate.warnings` list, with the op label. `ok` and `held_by` do not change, because the laws warn and do not refuse.
- `mcp/job.rs` (`verify`): each gate warning is a finding. The finding has the op label, `move: null`, the kind, the message and `blocks_post: false`.
- The `not_judged` line does not change. The G-code viewer header shows only this line, so the UI keeps the warnings.

## Cause

The plasma clause put its warnings into one sentence in `gate.not_judged`. Nothing else carried them. `findings`, the op `warnings` and `ok` read a clean program.

## Tests

- Pin: `mcp_plasma::plasma_mcp_verify_lists_a_tip_up_as_a_finding_and_an_operation_warning`. The test saves a cache with two parts. The rapid into C1 crosses the freed part C0. The test then runs MCP `verify`. It asserts one `plasma_tip_up` finding for `Plasma1` with `blocks_post: false`, the same text in the op `warnings`, no gate problem, an empty `held_by`, and `ok: true`.
- Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code, `findings` was `[]` and the warning was only in `not_judged` (`left: 0, right: 1`).
- Mutations (each run on the pin, then restored):
  - `mcp/job.rs` back to upstream/main: red (no finding).
  - The op-row push in `gate_warnings` removed: red (the op warnings assert).
  - The `GateWarning` push in `plasma_clause` removed: red (no finding).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `cd3669c58`: 307 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `mcp_plasma` and `plasma_gate`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a heavy step only to a `P1` PR.

## Goldens moved

None. I ran `git diff --stat upstream/main -- '*.nc' '*.cl' 'examples/catalog/**'`: no change. The example catalog suites pass. The change does not touch a generator or a post.

## Not exercised

- The QA project `q06-bracket.camproj` itself. The pin builds the same law result (a rapid over a freed part) on a small fixture.
- A kerf-crossing warning end to end. It uses the same code path as the tip-up; only the kind name is different.
- The UI. No UI code changed. The viewer header still reads `not_judged`.
- A change to the cut order or the rapid route that avoids the freed slugs. That is generator work. It is not in this PR.

## Overlaps

- #3611 changes `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` (`v_load`, `v_save`). This PR changes `v_verify`. The file is the same; the functions are different. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #3251 and #3103 change `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs` (`list_operation_types`). This PR changes `verify`. The file is the same; the functions are different.
- #2972, #2974, #2978, #2979, #2981, #2992, #2993 and #2999 change `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (Agie post functions). This PR changes `GateReport` and the end of `verification_report_by`. The file is the same; the functions are different.

title: fix(links): add the approach distance outside the stock for Inside and Outside passes
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/approach.rs`: a new field `Approach::approach_distance` (mm). The default is `DEFAULT_APPROACH_DISTANCE` = 2.0. `Approach::approach_distance_refusal()` refuses a negative, non-finite or too large value by name. `Approach::validate` calls it.
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs`: `named_refusal` gives that refusal, so `CreateOperation` and `EditOperationParams` refuse a bad value with its name. Before this, the refusal was only the general "operation parameters are not usable".
- `crates/app/src/project/approach.rs`: the optional file key `approach_distance`. The file writes it only when the value is not the default. A file without the key loads the default. The project format version does not change (the serde default law), so this change is not breaking.
- `crates/app/src/operation/params/digest.rs`: the digest adds bytes only for a value that is not the default. The digest of each earlier operation does not change.
- UI (`approach_page.rs`, `kind_editors.rs`, `mill2d_page.rs`): the Lead in / Lead out tab of 2D Offset, 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive shows an "Approach" group with the row "Approach distance" and a hover tooltip. The row shows only when Pass starts at is Inside or Outside.
- MCP: `edit_operation` and `add_operation` set the value through `links.approach.approach_distance` (the same params door, the same undoable command). `get_job` reads it. `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` has a new row.
- `docs/decisions/3745-approach-distance.md`: the default and its reason.

No change to the ring planner (#3744) or to the entry. The entry sub-issue #3746 reads the value. Until then the value is stored and changes no move.

## Pinning tests

- `mcp_approach_distance::approach_distance_default_is_two_mm_and_writes_no_key` (the default)
- `mcp_approach_distance::mcp_sets_approach_distance_and_refuses_a_negative_value` (MCP set and get; refusal of -1.0, -0.001 on edit and -2.0 on add, by name, with no change to the job)
- `mcp_approach_distance::approach_distance_edit_undoes_and_redoes` (undo and redo through `EditOperationParams`)
- `mcp_approach_distance::approach_distance_round_trips_through_save_and_load` (save and load keep the value; a file without the key loads the default)
- `lead_approach::the_stamp_tells_the_approach_apart_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_digest` (one new case: a changed approach distance changes the digest)
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::the_leads_tab_shows_the_approach_distance_only_for_inside_and_outside` (UI structural: the row is present for Inside and Outside, absent for Auto, on Pocket, Offset2D and Adaptive2D)

## Gate

- The pinning tests above: green (`cargo xtask gate test`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`).
- `lead_approach::the_approach_round_trips_and_the_defaults_write_no_key`: green.
- `ui suites: lib` (all camcraft-ui lib tests): green.
- `motion suites: lib`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the full quick plan. The motion diff reaches 1186 steps (every app and ui binary), so it is not a quick run. The batch gate on main covers it after the merge.
- Heavy lanes: not run. No toolpath or post output changes: the value has no reader yet.

## Not exercised

- No app window was opened. The tooltip text is not asserted (egui puts a hover text in the tree only on hover).
- 3D Pocket, 3D Finish, Bore and Circular do not show the row. #3746 decides which kinds read the value.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`)

Effort: high

body:
## What changed

Install an uncaptured-error handler when the shared GPU device is made.
Use one failure latch for this handler and the device-loss callback.
Keep the first reason and log it once.
Later stock-cut calls use the existing CPU path and return its exact values.

## Cause

The shared device had a device-loss callback but no uncaptured-error handler.
An unscoped validation error reached the default wgpu handler and caused a panic.

## Tests

Pin: `shared::tests::shared_device_faults_use_cpu`.
The pin runs each fault in an isolated process.
It checks real device destruction and an unscoped validation error.
It checks repeated CPU calls and retention of the first reason.
The unchanged code failed with the wgpu validation panic before the fix.

Mutation checks restore the old production code, remove each callback, and bypass the failure-refusal guard.
All four mutations fail the pin.
Each restored fix passes.

Final checks use upstream/main `0760e54ed` as the base:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-gpu --lib shared::tests::shared_device_faults_use_cpu -- --exact --nocapture`: passed.
  Both fault paths ran on llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 256 bits) through Vulkan.
  Neither path skipped.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed, 3 of 3 steps.
  The GPU library has 8 passing tests, including the pin.

title: fix(xtask): the recording build writes its JSON to a file, not a pipe
body:
## What changed

The gate's recording build (`debug build: <crate> (--no-run)`) now writes cargo's JSON to a file in the temporary directory. It does not use a pipe for it any more (`xtask/src/direct.rs`, `direct::cargo`).

## Cause

`direct::cargo` read the JSON through a pipe, in a reader thread. It joined that thread after cargo exited. A process that the build starts and that outlives the build inherits cargo's stdout. The sccache server is such a process: the first `rustc` wrapper call starts it when no server runs. That server keeps a copy of the write end of the pipe. The reader then got no end of file until the server stopped (its idle timeout). No watchdog runs during that join, because the watchdog stops when cargo exits. So the step waited after a green build. The wait depends on the sccache server state. The issue names a cargo "rmeta handoff". This worker did not see that wedge here. The pipe hold is the one wait of the prebuild path that depends on the sccache state, and the test below shows it.

The watchdog counts the file size (from the open handle) as output, as it counted the pipe bytes before. The gate reads the file when cargo exits and then deletes it. A descendant that holds the file cannot hold the gate. The decision record is `docs/decisions/3675-prebuild-json-file.md`.

## Readings

- Pinning test with the old `direct.rs`: FAILED, "the step must end when cargo exits: 120.0331239s". The 60 s watchdog did not fire.
- Pinning test with the fix: pass, in less than 1 s.

## Pinning test

- `watchdog_tests::a_recording_build_ends_when_cargo_exits_not_when_its_descendants_do`: a fake cargo (the test executable, mode `orphan`) writes JSON and exits at once. Its descendant holds its stdout and sleeps 120 s. The step must end in less than 30 s, green, with the JSON.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask`: 323 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- Heavy lanes: none reached (xtask only).

## Not exercised

- A full batch gate run on this machine. The shared sccache server already ran, so a cold server start was not available without stopping the shared server. A second, private sccache server (other port) failed its compiles ("connection was forcibly closed"). So the cold-server path did not run end to end. The reported wedge (cargo 1.99.1) was not seen on this machine (cargo 1.100.0). The pipe hold is the probable cause, not a confirmed one. If the wedge comes back with this fix, reopen #3675.
- `direct::record` still runs `cargo metadata` with a captured stdout. It builds nothing and was not changed.
- Linux and macOS: the change uses only `std::fs` and `std::process`.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: medium

Fixes #3675

title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps v77 -> v78: an older reader must refuse rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `the_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v78 round-trip,
  v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin).
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v78 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Not included (the issue stays open)

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing
  (decision part 3/4): the live claim on
  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's
  disagreement refusal keeps the radial kinds locked on helical
  parts until that kernel can consume the stated axis safely.
- No 360-degree radial drop finish for Rotary Parallel, no
  Doosan/Fanuc posting of one - same slice.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read a
stated rotation axis first (the operation's own direction, else the
machine's stated rotary line through the work offset origin), judged
against the model's faces - a part on the stated line cuts the fitted
path unchanged, a part whose faces disagree refuses by name (the
4-axis case named), and nothing stated keeps the fitted axis (v78
project files).

title: feat(gcode): add the camcraft-gcode reader crate for 3-axis RS-274 and ISO 6983 programs
body:
## What this PR does

This PR adds the new crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`). The crate reads RS-274/NGC and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs. It gives `cl::Toolpath` sections and a 1-based line map. It refuses unsupported words by name and line number.

- The crate depends on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry` and `thiserror` only.
- It decodes the modal groups, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs in `G17`/`G18`/`G19`, and the canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98`/`G99` and `L`.
- It splits sections at `T`/`M6`. It reads `S`, `M3`-`M5`, `M0`-`M2`, `M30`, `G4`, `G61`, `G64`, `G53`, `G28` and `G30`.
- It refuses `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, a missing `G20`/`G21`, a missing reference position, and `A`/`B`/`C`.

Sources: RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556), ISO 6983, and the public controller documents that `crates/gcode/src/dialect.rs` names for the dwell and arc presets. No other parser code was used.

## Held work

- Commit `711314efd` by Mike Kinney, from `mkinney:issue/2217-camcraft-gcode`. It has the crate, its 9 tests, the decision file and the gate plan entries.
- This PR keeps that commit and its author unchanged. A merge commit (`db23cf9bd`) joins it to main `60376ccbb`.

## Added after the held commit

- `db23cf9bd` merge: the conflict resolution (next section).
- `75b33ace3` `test(xtask)`: two xtask tests of main list the crates by hand. `heavy_plan_tests::reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies` now expects `gcode` in the reach of `geometry`. `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep` now writes a stub `crates/gcode`. `Cargo.lock` takes the version `0.25.0` for `camcraft-gcode`.
- `92627aef0` `test(gcode)`:
  - Each gcode suite has a `Gate map: covers camcraft_gcode::{..}` line. Quick then selects the suites for a change in each `crates/gcode/src` module.
  - The new suite `degenerate_input` checks malformed programs. Each one gives a value or a refusal, with no panic and no hang.
  - The decision file records the merge.

## Conflict resolution

All three conflicts were lists. No logic hunk had a conflict.

- Root `Cargo.toml`: the `members` line has main's `"crates/gpu"` and the held `"crates/gcode"` (after `"crates/cl"`). The `camcraft-gcode` workspace dependency merged without a conflict.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs`: `BATCH_CRATES`, `ALL_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` have `"gcode"` after `"cl"` and main's `"gpu"` after `"app"`.
- `xtask/src/tests.rs`: the release step count keeps main's known-fail `checks` term. It uses the held `plan::ALL_CRATES.len()` in place of the fixed `10`.
- `Cargo.lock` merged without a conflict.

## New crate edges

- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-cl`: `ArcPlane`, `Cycle`, `CycleKind`, `MoveKind`, `PathBuilder`, `Toolpath`, `lattice`.
- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-geometry`: `geo2d::Point2`, `Point3`, `units::{from_display, Unit, MM_PER_INCH}`.
- `docs/decisions/2217-camcraft-gcode.md` gives the imported items, the reason that a caller cannot pass the values in, and the rebuild impact. No crate depends on `camcraft-gcode` yet.

## Review fixes (review of `92627aef0`)

Commit `cb4acfadd` fixes the 11 review items. The merge `e0cc82c99` takes current `origin/main` (`44903e15e`); it merged with no conflict. The decision file has one entry for each item.

1. G73/G83: each peck must move deeper, at most 4096 pecks; one cycle block emits at most 100 000 moves.
2. Numeric domain: lengths and points are finite and inside +/-1e6 mm after conversion and arithmetic; caller options are checked. New errors `OutOfRange` and `InvalidOptions`.

All tests are in one directory suite, `crates/gcode/tests/parse/` (`main.rs` holds the Gate map and the shared 5 s time-limit helper). No new top-level test binary. The `#[test]` count went from 10 to 37.

- `frames` (item 3): `g54_to_g55_keeps_the_machine_move`, `nonzero_origins_move_the_cursor_on_every_axis`, `offset_change_after_motion_without_origins_refuses`, `g28_and_g30_use_the_machine_origin_of_the_active_offset`, `g28_without_a_known_work_origin_refuses`.

title: feat(multiaxis): Rotary Flow kernel - flow lines between picked helical guide chains
body:
## What changed

The first slice of the Rotary Flow kind (issue #2824, part of #2804): a 4-axis cylindrical flow-line kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`, split over four files under the 400-line law.

- `rotary_flow.rs` - the public entry. `rotary_flow(chains, facets, ax, p, c)` takes the picked guide chains, the part facets, the STATED rotation axis (the #2772 seam - the axis is a parameter, never fitted here), `RotaryFlowParams` and `AxisControl`. The params carry the `Tool` itself, so the ball-nose requirement is refused by name. Clearance and retract read as ball-center radii about the axis.
- `rotary_flow_unwrap.rs` - each chain unwound to a continuous `(theta, v)` track (the radian twin of `cl::unwrap_near`), each adjacent pair aligned by the nearest whole turn, the band developed `(s = R_ref * theta, v)` with `R_ref` the chains' outermost radius, and the picked-chain ground checks (finite, distinct, on-model, off-axis).
- `rotary_flow_pass.rs` - the iso-parametric flow curves between the aligned pair, each station's ball center pushed out along its radial until the `closest_pt_tri` oracle clears every facet (march, then bisect), the curve chorded within `min(ARC_FIT_TOL, tolerance)` over the union of the two chains' arc-length knots.
- `rotary_flow_emit.rs` - tips via the pivot law (`retip`), cut poses through the lean law on the radial (`tilt`), links rebuilt radially on the retract cylinders (`rotary_links`' law: feed retract, chorded index short way round, radial plunge), the program opening on the clearance pose (M13.8).

Refusals by name: a tool that is not a ball-nose, fewer than two chains, a non-finite point, a point off the model, a point on the axis line, chains wound in opposite senses, a band with no width, a stepover or tolerance at the scallop ceiling (the finishing kinds' own law), a station the push-out cannot clear within five radii, a pass count over the 4096-pass ceiling, a clearance that does not clear the work.

The decisions taken unattended are in `docs/decisions/2824-rotary-flow-kernel.md`: the `Tool`-carrying params (the drilling precedent), the ball-center radius reading of the heights, `R_ref` at the chains' outermost radius (ground inside it gets finer, never coarser), and one band per adjacent chain pair with both edge passes kept (a shared middle chain is walked once per band - the re-cut is the same geometry at the same depth).

## The readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 29 steps, 0 failed - motion lib, `multiaxis`, `rotary`, the new `rotary_flow` binary, and the reached app suites (operations, posed_contact, rotary_fixtures, rotary_verify, and the rest). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the rotor groove fixture: the developed band reads 4.000 mm at R 8.000 mm; 6 flow passes at a 0.9 mm stepover; the first pass rides the wall push-out (rho about 11), interior passes ride the floor a ball radius off it; every cut station's ball keeps its radius off the part.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow/rotary_flow_tests.rs` (15 tests): every refusal by name (non-ball tool, chain count, empty model, off-model at its spot, on-axis, degenerate band, opposite senses, both scallop ceilings, low clearance), the pass count law, `align_pair`'s nearest whole turn, `lerp_at`, `unwrap_near`, and a small on-model band that poses, clears and opens at clearance.
- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_flow.rs` (3 run, 1 heavy): `a_rotor_floor_band_flows_multi_turn_without_gouge` (the no-gouge pin over every station against `camcraft_sim`'s own `dist_seg_tri`, multi-turn span, wall vs floor riders), `a_pair_straddling_the_branch_aligns_by_a_whole_turn` (same pass count as the unshifted band, the note stating the shift), `climb_reverses_each_pass`, and the ignored `the_rotor_envelope_stays_gouge_free_at_the_scallop_law` (heavy lane: release --ignored, the 4-turn fine rotor envelope scanned station by station).

## What was not exercised

- The app layer, the command and the MCP tool are owed to the #2804 sub-issues; this PR changes only the motion kernel.
- The whole-turn alignment is pinned by the kernel basis' own branch (e1 = +Y on a Z axis); a pair straddling a different frame's branch reaches the same law through the same shift.
- A band whose pair meets at a whole-turn boundary exactly (offset = half a lap) is not tested; the nearest-turn law would pick either side.
- `graphify update` did not run: the `graphify` command is not on this session's PATH.
- Heavy lane: only the ignored envelope scan touches it; it runs at the cut.

Changelog: multiaxis: Rotary Flow - a 4-axis flow-line finishing kernel between picked helical guide chains on a stated rotation axis

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- Skims on an open run are not judged per pass by the wire verify (it
  refuses them by name); a follow-up can split the passes and judge
  each at its own kerf.
- Taper, burnout and 4-axis cuts do not read the overlap; each refuses
  an open run or walks the closed lap as before.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

Changelog: Wire Contour: a stated closing overlap rides the cut past its seam; a centre-line slit side for open runs; skim passes on open runs re-entered from the air.

title: feat: open a project read-only with --read-only and open_project read_only
body:
## What changed

`camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens a project read-only. The MCP
tool `open_project` takes `read_only: true` for the same result. A save
over the opened file is then refused on every save route, and the file
stays byte for byte. A save to another file works and ends read-only. The
title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.

- One rule, `project::refuse_read_only_save` in `crates/app/src/project/`,
  refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The
  window's `State::save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it.
  `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP
  seam of a window.
- The rule compares canonical paths, so a save from the Save As dialog
  to the opened file is refused too.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as
  the editor for shipped machines does. The Save of the unsaved-changes
  prompt does the same.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- The read-only state is kept next to the document path:
  `State::project_read_only` in the window, `Env::doc_read_only` in a
  headless MCP session or a script run. The live seam gets the window's
  state through `LiveOptions::read_only`.
- A model file with `--read-only` is imported as usual. A headless start
  ignores the option. The live seam still refuses `open_project`.
- The same option name and behaviour as the open SolidCraft proposal
  for `--read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830).
- No change to the file format or `PROJECT_VERSION`.
- Docs: the `--help` text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`,
  `site/content/guide/automate/cli.md` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3609-read-only-open.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`. Two merges of upstream
main follow it: `b94dcd378` (main `82db54282`) and `98cd5b28b` (main
`3fc0e017b`). There is no rebase.

- The first merge had conflicts with #3608 (overwrite guard) and #3584
  (start options). Both sides added lines in the same places. The merge
  keeps both sides.
- In `v_save` and `State::save_project_path`, the read-only check runs
  first, and then the overwrite guard of #3608. Thus `overwrite: true`
  does not write over a file that is open read-only.
- `--read-only` comes after `--no-activate` and `--minimized` in the
  options table, the `--help` text and `start-options.md`.
  `run_windowed` takes the start mode and `read_only`.
- `LiveOptions` and `Env` have `read_only` and `doc_stamp`. The
  `save_project` description has the sentences of both changes.
- `crates/app/tests/save_overwrite_guard.rs` gets one line,
  `read_only: false`, in its `LiveOptions` value. This is the only line
  outside the files of this change.
- The second merge had no conflicts. It brings in #3687 (a relative
  model link resolves against the project folder).

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/read_only_open.rs`:

- `the_rule_refuses_only_the_opened_file_of_a_read_only_project`
- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_keeps_it`
- `a_save_to_another_file_works_and_ends_read_only`
- `a_plain_open_ends_read_only_and_a_bad_flag_changes_nothing`
- `a_script_save_after_a_read_only_open_is_refused`
- `the_live_seam_refuses_an_approved_save_over_a_read_only_window_project`

New in `crates/ui/src/launch_file_tests.rs`:

- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_save_as_ends_read_only`
- `read_only_changes_nothing_for_a_model_file`

New in `crates/ui/src/cli_options_tests.rs`:

- `read_only_is_a_switch_that_keeps_the_file_after_it`

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head `98cd5b28b`
(Windows 11). The diff since main `3fc0e017b` is 23 files. 226 of 229
steps passed, and 0 stalled. The three red steps are not from this
change:

- `example_catalog`: `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::{rebuilds,regenerates}`.
  The refusal text is equal, and only the line end is different. The
  checkout uses `core.autocrlf=true`, so `refusal.txt` has `\r\n`.
- `catalog_render`: `catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly`. The case
  `3d/rough-finish` links `model/rough-finish.obj`. With
  `core.autocrlf=true` the file on disk has `\r\n`, so its sha256 is not
  the one in the project, and the link check imports it again. The blob
  in git has the sha256 of the project.
- `first_router_part`:
  `first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal`. Main
  is red with this step (#3698).

The steps of this change and of #3608 all passed:

- `read_only_open`: 6 passed.
- `save_overwrite_guard`: 7 passed.
- `mcp_live`: 14 passed.
- `mcp_doc_drift`: 6 passed.
- `mcp`: 29 passed.
- `scripting`: 20 passed.
- `project_roundtrip`: 80 passed.
- `first_part_programs`: 2 passed (#3574 is fixed on main).
- The app lib tests: 303 passed.
- The `camcraft-ui` lib tests: 1524 passed, 8 ignored. These include
  `launch_file_tests` and `cli_options_tests`.
- 15 of the 16 ui suites passed, among them `gpu_render`, `shell` and
  `operations`. The red one is `catalog_render` (above).

The other app steps are the suites that the gate maps from
`app::project`, `app::script` and `app::mcp`.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
on `98cd5b28b`: clean (exit 0). The only warning is the manifest note about the unused workspace dependency `truck-polymesh`, which is not from this change.
Heavy lanes: not run (no heavy step for a `P2` or lower PR, #3556).
Reach from `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` at `144d07a85`: every `app`
heavy target (212 steps), because `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs` changed.

## Manual check

Windows 11, debug build of `98cd5b28b`. A person did the keyboard and
dialog steps. The window title and the files were read through Windows
and on disk.

1. `camcraft-ui --read-only edge-work.camproj`, a copy of
   `examples/catalog/2d/edge-work`. The title is
   `CamCraft - edge-work.camproj (read-only)`. The status line says
   `opened ... (read-only; Save As writes your own copy)`. The file does
   not change.
2. Ctrl+S opens the Save As dialog.
3. Save As to the same file: Windows asks to replace the file, and the
   user selects yes. CamCraft refuses the save. The status line shows
   `save refused: ... is open read-only; write your copy to a different
   file` in red. The file does not change: the sha256 and the
   modification time are the same.
4. A change to the machine sets the unsaved mark `*` in the title. The
   change stays in memory.
5. Save As to a new file writes `edge-work-copy.camproj`. The title
   becomes `CamCraft - edge-work-copy.camproj`, without `(read-only)` and
   without `*`. The first file does not change.

Finding, not changed in this PR: after the user says yes to the replace
prompt, the user expects a write. The refusal shows only on the status
line, and a narrow window cuts the line. The user in this check did not
see the refusal. A possible follow-up is a notice that the user must
close.

## Not in this change

- A read-only open on the live seam. The live seam refuses
  `open_project`, so that an agent cannot skip the window's
  unsaved-changes prompt. The window's read-only state still reaches a
  live `save_project`.
- A new script form `cam.load(path, options)`. Scripts use
  `cam.call("open_project", {path, read_only: true})`.
- `read_only` in `get_job`.
- The window does not follow the path of a live `save_project` with a
  new path. This is the behaviour today. The window keeps its path and
  stays read-only.
- A reopen from the recent list, or in a later session, is not
  read-only. The recent list keeps paths only.
- The read-only bit of the file on disk.
- A hand-off of the flag to a running window. CamCraft has no
  single-instance hand-off.

## Not exercised

- An automated test of the Save As dialog route in the window. A
  headless test cannot open a native dialog. The tests pin the refusal
  behind it, and the manual check above did the route by hand.
- The live seam through a real window and the AI chat's Allow prompt.
  A test calls `answer_live_with` with the options that the window builds.
- Linux and macOS.
- A project on a network share.
- No test sets a project read-only and then calls `save_project` with
  `overwrite: true` over its own file. The order of the two checks
  (read-only first) is in the code, but no test pins it.

Changelog: `camcraft-ui --read-only` and `open_project` with `read_only: true` open a project read-only: Save never writes over the opened file, and Save As writes your own copy.
