title: fix(2d): note the corner reliefs that get no spur
body:
## What changed

A planned corner relief whose start no pass vertex reaches, and for which no legal detour exists, was dropped without a diagnostic (#3249). It could leave material the operator does not expect.

- `inject_relief_spurs` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs`) now reports each skipped relief: the caller gets the boundary corners in a `misses` vector.
- The pocket emit path (`pocket_emit.rs`) and the pocket avoid path (`pocket_avoid.rs`) write one note per corner into the `PathBuilder` / path notes: `corner relief at (x, y) is not cut: no pass vertex reaches the relief spur`. Notes are de-duplicated by corner, so a multi-level cut or a retry names each corner once.
- The four-dogbones rest test keeps its no-note assert: a reached relief adds no note.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket corner relief that no pass reaches is now named in the operation notes instead of being dropped silently.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::corner_relief_spur::tests::a_relief_no_pass_reaches_is_reported_as_a_miss` (crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs): the miss is reported and no spur is spliced in; a reached relief reports no miss and gets its spur.
- `unreachable_corners_and_bad_overrides_are_refused` (crates/motion/tests/corner_relief.rs): the island-blocked spur refuses at plan time.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_corner_relief.rs`: the rest pass keeps its no-note assert.

## Review fix

The miss vector uses `r.corner`, the boundary corner, instead of `r.start`, the cutter-center start.
Both existing callers use the returned corners for duplicate detection.

- The existing miss pin now uses corner `(0,0)` and start `(3,3)`.
- `machining2d::pocket_emit::tests::missed_relief_notes_name_and_deduplicate_boundary_corners` checks the resulting path notes.
  It checks equal corners with different starts and different corners with an equal start.

## Review fix validation

Final head: `1814e1119b8fdbf86f1f6a4fe8b245b9a30286e0`.
Base: `9dfcc7ac2ae59c30a43796382968b4cba93970e5` (`upstream/main`).

The base was fetched before these checks. Upstream advanced during the run to `6167d30af724eb8fa8904b6744c26cd295ff08dd`.
After fetching that head, both dry plans were compared with the recorded base.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects the same nine step names and commands.
`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects the same 243 step names and commands.
`git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD` lists the same five files for both bases.
The completed checks cover every step selected against current upstream/main. No additional step was selected.
The actual runs used base `9dfcc7ac2ae59c30a43796382968b4cba93970e5`. A merge with newer main was not exercised.

The miss vector now contains boundary corners. Existing callers use these points to remove duplicate notes.
The path-note test checks equal corners with different starts and different corners with an equal start.

Pin proof:

- `machining2d::corner_relief_spur::tests::a_relief_no_pass_reaches_is_reported_as_a_miss`
- `machining2d::pocket_emit::tests::missed_relief_notes_name_and_deduplicate_boundary_corners`

Each pin passed with the fix. Changing `misses.push(r.corner)` back to `misses.push(r.start)` made both pins fail.
The first pin reported `(3,3)` instead of `(0,0)`. The path-note pin reported `(3,3)` and `(4,3)` instead of `(0,0)` and `(10,0)`.
Restoring the fix made both pins pass again. Commands used `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib <full_test_name> -- --exact`.

body:
## What changed

Two gaps in the gate's unit sweep (#3173). The sweep's verdict logic is untouched.

1. A link at the package level: the scan already skipped a package directory
   that is a link, but no test covered it. New test
   `unit_sweep_tests::a_link_at_the_package_level_is_skipped`: the scan does not
   enter the link, the sweep removes nothing through it, and the link itself
   stays.
2. Case folding on a case-insensitive volume: `norm` folded case only on
   Windows, so on the case-insensitive default volume of macOS a link target or
   canonical path that differs only by case missed the process-check needles.
   `norm` now folds case on macOS too. New test
   `a_path_that_differs_only_by_case_is_one_form_on_a_case_insensitive_volume`
   pins the fold (and pins that a case-sensitive Unix volume keeps the
   difference).

## Readings

title: fix(2d): support Do not touch on 2D Pocket operations
body:
Was stacked on #3353, which has merged.

## What changed

- Add `OpType::Pocket` to `do_not_touch_applies` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`.
- Update `do_not_touch_unsupported` to list all supported kinds: 2D Pocket, Trace, 2D Offset, 2D Adaptive, 3D Pocket, Face, 3D Finish and Engrave.
- Update the `set_operation_do_not_touch` text in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Wire `OpParams::Pocket` with `avoid_spec` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` to `pocket_avoid_entered_started`, `rest_pocket_avoid_with_relief`, and `rest_pocket_previous_avoid_with_relief`.
- Extract per-level planning (`plan_avoid_level`), relief checks (`check_reliefs_avoid`), crossing-free checks (`enforce_level_crossing_free`), and rest dispatch (`emit_rest_avoid`) into `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid_level.rs`.
- Unify plain and rest avoid paths in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, and `rest_prior.rs` under `pocket_avoid_over`.
- Check overhead keep-out zones up to `p.clearance_z.max(z)` so entry rapids and final clearance lifts clear overhead obstacles.
- Guard `Descent::Helix` (`m.solid_restart`) and `entry_restart` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs` and `descent_dive.rs` with `helix_clears_prior`, `find_clear_helix_raw`, `moves_clear`, and `helix_cross_fallback`.
- Record between-pass `KeepDown` chords in `LinkState.level` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs`.
- Derive `Clone` for `LinkTally`, `LinkState`, and `WalkState`.
- Add pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/avoid_pocket.rs`, `crates/app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`, and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`.
- Record the design choice in `docs/decisions/3345-do-not-touch-2d-pocket.md`.

## Cause

- `do_not_touch_applies` refused `OpType::Pocket`, and `OpParams::Pocket` in `generate.rs` dropped `avoid_spec`.
- `pocket_avoid` supported plain 2D Offset only. It lacked `PreHole` entries and rest plans, and it checked overhead obstacles only up to `retract_z`.
- When keep-out zones trimmed inner passes across depths under `OffsetRings` + `KeepDown` + `Helix`, restarted helices overlapped earlier helices in XY at shared entry depths.

## Tests

- Before the fix, `pocket2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge` failed in `set_operation_do_not_touch`.
- Before the fix, `pocket2d_boundaries_shows_pick_protected_and_takes_viewport_click` panicked on the missing `"Pick protected"` button.

title: fix(multiaxis): rotate the rotaries before the first five-axis approach descent
body:
﻿## What changed

Five-axis generators set the first station's pose on the modal builder
and then pushed the descend to first contact, so the rotary swing rode
the approach move: the machine turned the A/C head while the tool
descended, and the ball swept through unknown air and through the rim
it approached.

The fix splits the approach. The pose is stated as its own zero-travel
Rapid (a standstill rotary index - the tip held on the hop plane, or at
the tip the machine already holds), and the Plunge/cut descends under
the pose already stated:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve.rs` (`contour_curve`): every
  chain's approach swings first, then plunges.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs` (the stamp emit loop, all
  posed kinds - parallel5d, flow5d, swarf5d, rough, contour5d): at
  every rapid-to-cut re-entry where the pose changes, the swing is
  emitted at a standstill before the cut. Intermediate cut moves keep
  the modal tilt law unchanged.

No new `MoveKind`. The builder already keeps a zero-travel move whose
pose changed (it drops one only when the tip AND the pose both stand),
and the post already solves a zero-travel segment as a pure rotary
reorientation (`ds_tip == 0` in `crates/post/src/post/g93.rs`), so the
swing always commands. That is the answer to the zero-travel question:
the swing is a zero-travel rapid, not a short travel move - a travel
move would drag the tip sideways while the head turns, and a dropped
zero-travel move cannot occur, because a drop needs the pose to match
the held one, in which case no rotation is due.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 28 steps, 0 failed
  (motion lib 536 passed, multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough,
  pivot5d, swarf_pose_continuity, app operations, posed_contact and the
  rest all green).
- The existing laws were amended where the swing touches them, each in
  its own terms: a TRAVEL rapid still inherits its pose
  (`rapids_hold_the_pose_they_inherit`, `rapid_pose_contract` - the
  zero-travel index is the second legal way a rapid states a pose,
  beside the swarf link's ball-centred swing); the air-link ratchet
  counts travel links only; the pivot-law ball readers skip the
  swing (it cuts nothing) through `no_swings`/`sans_swings` helpers.
- A decision record sits in `docs/decisions/3414-approach-rotary-order.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `the_approach_rotates_before_it_descends` (crates/motion/tests/pivot5d.rs):
  a zero-travel rotary swing precedes the first descend; the plunge
  holds the pose the swing stated; no pose change rides any move that
  crosses from air to material, over contour_curve, parallel5d, flow5d
  and swarf5d.

## What was not exercised

- No posted G-code golden was regenerated (the post's pure-rotary path
  is covered by its own suite; the swing was not posted end to end on
  a real machine file).
- The heavy lanes were not run; the diff touches `camcraft-motion`, so
  the release-tier lane check stays with the review/cut.

New test binary reason: `crates/app/tests/approach_rotary_order.rs` pins, at the app level, that the five-axis approach rotates the machine to the first pose before the tool descends; no existing app suite covers the approach ordering across rotary words, so the pin takes a binary of its own.

## Changelog

Five-axis approach moves rotate the machine to the first pose before
the tool descends to the part, no longer while it descends.

Fork synced at v0.25.0.

Fixes #3414

title: fix(multiaxis): close the Rotary Offset Zigzag levels with a ring that skips the seam
body:
## What changed

Rotary Offset Zigzag levels now finish their walls with a ring, as the
planar #3129 levels already do. On the wrap the plan drops only the
seam's own edges: a boundary loop that spans a whole period wraps the
seam, and its two cover-end edges are the seam's two copies at one
azimuth. That loop's ring keeps one period of boundary per leftover arc;
each arc arrives open and ends on the seam copy of its start azimuth -
closed on the work - while the rows cut the seam columns. A loop that
wraps no azimuth closes exactly as the planar ring always did. The
no-seam path is byte-for-byte the old `zigzag_ringed_passes` behaviour.

Before the fix the wrap kept its rows alone, so every wall perpendicular
to the rows kept cusps between row ends. Measured on the new test's
D-flat: the worst wall scallop falls from 0.071 mm to under 0.02 mm at
every level between the flat and the skin.

Placement: `machining2d::pocket_zigzag::ringed_passes` (the seam law,
one `Option<f64>` period), called from `machining3d::hsm::plan_level`.
Decision record: `docs/decisions/3168-rotary-zigzag-seam-rings.md`.

## Pinning tests

New suite `crates/motion/tests/rotary_zigzag_rings.rs`:

- `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` - on a developed cover two
  periods wide, the target band's ring cuts every azimuth once: no
  azimuth bin takes radial feed runs in both directions, and the band's
  walls stay within the wall-reach bound. This is the failure the old
  "a ring there would cut one seam line twice" comment feared.
- `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` - a D-flat bar wraps and its edge
  walls (perpendicular to the rows) finish within the wall-reach bound
  at every level between the flat and the skin. Run against the unfixed
  tree it fails with `scallop 0.071 mm`.

## What was not exercised

- The Adaptive seam law (`Seam::crossed_by`, the named refusals) is
  untouched and its own suites still cover it.
- No posted G-code golden was re-recorded; the change alters Zigzag
  wrap toolpaths by adding rings, which the level law's own tests do not
  pin.
- The heavy lanes reached by a `motion` diff were not run locally; the
  review runs them per AGENTS.md.

Changelog: Rotary Offset Zigzag levels finish their walls with a closing
ring that skips the seam, removing wall cusps on flats and other
perpendicular walls.

Fixes #3168

title: feat(motion): engrave and trace open and closed sketch chains
body:
Engrave and Trace now follow open and closed chains from a placed sketch. The user can select a profile, individual chains or a layer. The operation preserves the cut direction of lines, arcs and circles. It applies the sketch placement and the work-coordinate rotation to both endpoints and arc centers. A lift separates disconnected strokes and gaps accepted by the drawing tolerance.

Each depth level approaches from the stock surface. The existing stock, fixture, shank and mark-depth checks can hold the post, including jobs that have no part solid. Very short arcs below the post resolution give a diagnostic. A major arc is split into two arcs that keep its center and sweep. #3442 tracks the separate case where a native Fanuc post accepts a short arc supplied directly in an intermediate file.

The 18-move CL fixture contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden moves. One new recorded file is added.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/sketch_engrave_trace.cl` (NEW, not moved)

The new CL file records 18 moves. It contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes. The test `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` compares the generated moves with this file.

## Verification

- On the parent source, `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` failed because an operation could not use picked sketch chains. The same test passed on this fix. The original CLI also refused both Engrave and Trace on a whole profile.
- On `2032dda7e`, all 11 feature tests passed. The 18 moves matched the checked-in golden. The stock depth, underside, stock rapid, crossing and fixture checks held the post when required. Project round-trip and MCP passed.
- `short_and_near_full_arcs_keep_their_center_and_sweep_through_a_rotated_work_offset` checks the arc centers and sweeps. The native CLI generated, verified and posted six synthetic drawings across both operations. Short representable arcs kept distinct endpoints. The 270-degree and near-full sweeps used split arcs with the correct centers. Both sub-resolution cases gave a named refusal and wrote no NC file.
- The focused gate passed 480 app tests, 127 post tests, and 29 motion tests on the final commit. Strict Clippy passed for all app, motion, and post targets with warnings denied. A broader motion run passed 646 tests with 10 ignored on the earlier branch revision with identical motion source.
- The broad quick plan was a dry run. The focused app, motion and post suites and strict Clippy ran on this head. All 243 selected release-mode execution steps completed. They recorded 105 passing ignored tests and 4 registered expected failures. Of the selected steps, 206 had no ignored cases to run. Each selected suite compiled on demand. The separate aggregate compile-only step was omitted.

The CLI checks used synthetic drawings and the native post. No physical machine ran the resulting programs.

- Merge base: `origin/main` `3c68dcaf2`. Merge commit: `173abf61b`.

title: feat(wire): export a selected Agie opening for zero-step inspection
body:
The DXF import and Wire Contour selection prerequisites merged in #3193 and #3205. This PR adds the native zero-step inspection export.

The maintainer confirmed that the dependency and Agie-CAM reference approvals from #2951 also apply here. This PR gets its own safety review and trial-merge test after #2951 merges. [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3219#issuecomment-7080044891)

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

## Verification on head `d12d6e331` (merge of main `6167d30af`)

Commit `d12d6e331` merges main at `6167d30af` (#3731). The only conflict was the generated file `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`. I generated it again with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- mcp reference`. Against main, it adds only the two tools of this PR (`export_agie_inspection`, `create_agie_inspection`), and the tool count goes from 121 to 123.

- `app suites: mcp_doc_drift`: ok.
- `app suites: mcp_dxf`: ok.

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

The SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads drawings into the DXF `Document` type. It shares sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, sketch entities, and project storage with DXF import.

- Read paths, lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, and ellipses.
- Apply group transforms and references to elements in the same file.
- Keep circular arcs analytic. Flatten Beziers and other ellipses within 0.005 mm.
- Read mm, cm, in, pt, pc, and px sizes, `viewBox`, and `preserveAspectRatio`.
- Reflect Y about the page height. Use top-level group labels or IDs as layers.
- Count unsupported content, hidden content, markers and paint-only stylesheets as skipped. This includes stylesheets inside `<defs>`.
- Add the undoable `ImportSvg` command, the `import_svg` MCP tool, and the `cam.importSvg` script verb.
- Update the user guide and MCP reference. Record decisions in `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals

The reader names malformed input, unsupported units, invalid sizes, singular transforms, and exceeded import limits. A file without physical units needs the caller's unit. A sized file refuses a caller unit.

The reader also refuses root `<svg>` transform attributes, and `transform-origin` and `transform-box` presentation attributes.

The reader finds a duplicate attribute name with a map. The scan that it replaces was quadratic in the attribute count of one tag.

The reader reads an inline `style` against an allow-list of the properties that cannot change geometry (`SAFE_PROPERTIES` in `svg/facts.rs`). The reader refuses each other property by name. The reader reads the style and the transform of an element one time, finds a `use` target in a map of the ids, and charges the shape data of each visit against a work budget.

These rules close the class "an input changes or hides a shape, and the import ignores it":

- A `<style>` sheet is checked with the same allow-list, with no selector matching (`svg/sheet.rs`). The reader refuses `display`, `visibility` and each property that is not on the list. A paint-only sheet imports.
- The reader refuses an `<?xml-stylesheet?>` instruction and a `<link rel="stylesheet">` by name.
- The reader refuses `animate`, `set`, `animateTransform`, `animateMotion`, `animateColor` and `discard` at each place in the tree.
- A child of a shape or of a `use` that is not `title`, `desc`, `metadata` or `style` is counted as `<child> in <parent>`.
- The reader refuses a `preserveAspectRatio` value that is not in the SVG grammar.
- A marker property that draws a marker is counted as `marker`.
- The user guide says that a shape with a stroke imports as its centre line.

## The fix round for the review on `f96ea8fa0`

1. **One CSS scanner for the inline style and the sheet (`svg/css.rs`, new).** `sheet.rs` and `style.rs` take their pieces from it, so the two cannot split a style at different places.
   - An unquoted `url(` token ends at the first `)` that is not escaped, as in CSS Syntax 3 (4.3.6). In it, a quote starts no string, a `(` adds no level, and a `;`, a brace or a `/*` starts nothing.
   - `url` is found in any case and through escapes (`\75rl(`). `url(` before a quote is a function with a string, and the usual rules apply.
   - A bad url token (a quote, a `(` or a gap in the address) is refused by name: in a sheet at each place (a rule, an `@font-face` block, a prelude), and in the inline style of an imported element.
   - If the same inline style has `display:none`, the shape is hidden as in a browser. Nothing of it is imported, and it is counted as `hidden`.
2. **One function for references (`svg/reference.rs`, new).** After an `&`, the run goes to the first `;`, white space, `&`, `<` or quote. A run that ends at a `;` is a reference.
   - A reference is decoded only if it is one of the five predefined entities, or a character reference to a character that XML permits. The count of leading zeros has no limit.
   - Each other reference is refused by name: an entity name with a character outside ASCII, a run that is not an XML name (`&a=b;`, `A`), a code point that is not a character (`�`, `�`).
   - The namespace exception stays: the value of `xmlns` and `xmlns:*` is not read. A CDATA section has no references.
   - The scan is linear: the next search starts after the run.
3. **Directory suites.** This PR adds no new top-level test binary to a crate that has a directory suite for it.
   - `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` is now `crates/app/tests/mcp/svg.rs`, a module of the existing `mcp` suite. Its 2 tests are the same.
   - The four files `svg_refusals.rs`, `svg_style_safety.rs`, `svg_tree_rules.rs` and `svg_visibility.rs` are now modules in `crates/geometry/tests/svg/`. The two new pin files are there too.
   - New top-level test file: `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs`. Reason: `crates/geometry/tests/` had no directory suite for the SVG reader, and this file is the root of the new one (one binary in place of five).
   - `#[test]` count of the SVG suite: 61 before (16 + 19 + 6 + 9 + 11), 74 now. The 13 more are the new pins.

One existing pin changed its expected text. `.a{fill:url(a}b);transform:scale(2)}` was refused as "style sheet has a ';' outside a rule". The scanner now reads the `}` as a part of the address, and the reader refuses the file as "style sheet transform".

## Validation on the final head

Head: `ccb0ed35486a1689323753d5efc0b757b959fa39`. It has one commit after `245e84fa1`: a merge of `upstream/main` `074c23ba6`. The head `245e84fa1` had no review, thus this push has no review finding.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 1,190 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled, 20.5 minutes. The red step is `app suites: rotary_verify`; see below |
| `clippy -D warnings` | PASS: a step of the quick gate |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 98 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 17.8 minutes |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | PASS in the quick gate |
| `app suites: mcp` (has `mcp/svg.rs`), `mcp_doc_drift` | PASS in the quick gate |
| `geometry suites: svg` | PASS in the quick gate |

**The red step is the red step of main.** `rotary_verify::a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` fails (2110 moves, expected 2064). Issue #3774 records the same failure of the post-merge gate on main `074c23ba6`. This PR changes no rotary, motion or sim file. This PR does not correct it.

**Merge of main.** The merge `ccb0ed354` had one conflict.

- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (a generated file). I wrote it again with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- mcp reference`. It has 124 tools: the 123 tools of main and `import_svg`.
- The merge has no other hand edit. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is the file of main.

Main moved to `f6716cdcd` during the gates. `git merge-tree` of this head with that main is clean. The gates did not run against that main.

The gate light did not run again in this round. The earlier merge `3178256d7` (main `6167d30af`) and its gates are in the PR comments.

**Pin proof.** (From the round on `245e84fa1`; the merge changes no code of this PR, and I did not run the mutations again.) For each row, I made the mutation, ran `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test svg`, and restored the code. With the code restored, all 74 tests pass.

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| The scanner does not read `url(` tokens (`css.rs`: the `url(` arm is off). This is the behaviour before the fix. | `url_tokens::svg_style_sheet_bad_url_tokens_are_refused_by_name`, `url_tokens::svg_font_face_block_with_a_bad_url_token_is_refused_by_name`, `url_tokens::svg_inline_bad_url_tokens_are_refused_by_name_on_a_shape_a_group_and_the_root`, `url_tokens::svg_inline_display_none_after_a_bad_url_token_hides_the_shape`, `url_tokens::svg_a_comment_start_in_a_url_token_hides_no_declaration`, `url_tokens::svg_good_url_tokens_import_at_the_attribute_size`, `tree_rules::svg_style_sheet_rules_that_hide_or_resize_a_shape_are_refused_by_name` |
| A reference that is not a character stays as text, and a character reference with more than 9 digits is not decoded (`reference.rs`). This is the behaviour before the fix. | `references::svg_entity_names_outside_ascii_are_refused_at_each_place`, `references::svg_a_run_that_is_not_an_xml_name_is_refused_when_it_ends_at_a_semicolon`, `references::svg_character_references_with_leading_zeros_are_decoded_in_an_attribute`, `references::svg_character_references_with_leading_zeros_are_decoded_in_a_style_sheet`, `references::svg_character_references_that_are_not_a_character_are_refused_by_name`, `tree_rules::svg_doctype_entity_references_are_refused_by_name` |

These pins stay green in the two mutations, because they pin what must still import: `references::svg_predefined_and_plain_references_read_as_before`, `references::svg_many_reference_starts_read_in_linear_time`, and the usual `url(data:font/woff2;base64,AAAA)` rule in `tree_rules::svg_paint_only_style_sheets_import_at_the_attribute_size`.

The pins of the earlier rounds are in `tests/svg/tree_rules.rs`, `style_safety.rs`, `refusals.rs` and `visibility.rs`. Their mutation table is in the review record of `671426992`. I did not run those mutations again in this round.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog suites ran and passed on the final head. The diff against `upstream/main` changes no recorded program, golden or snapshot PNG.

## Not exercised

- I did not check the url and reference cases in a browser. The expected results are from CSS Syntax 3 and XML 1.0.
- The three follow-ups of the review on `f96ea8fa0` are not in this round: `<!ATTLIST` defaults of the DOCTYPE (`P3`), `systemLanguage` and `requiredExtensions` (`P3`), and a count of `<script>` and event attributes (`P7`). The review says to file them after the merge.
- A sheet scan does not follow `(` and `[` levels across a `}`. I examined this, and each case that I found is refused, not imported. It has no pin of its own.
- A posted G-code golden for an SVG profile remains in follow-up #3042.
- The `import_svg` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` remains outside this PR.
- Nested SVG viewports, selector matching of a style sheet, text to outlines, and embedded images remain outside this reader's scope.
- The merge with main `f6716cdcd` is not built and not gated. The merged main is `074c23ba6`.
- The description of the `import_svg` MCP tool is not changed.
- The four follow-ups of the first review on `eaafd2e72` (Inkscape long style, `vector-effect` attribute, the 5 s time limits, the skill row) are not changed.

No UI source changed. Before/after screenshots do not apply.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...814dca499f9f9793f3c9e6bcd3eafab5f32e2022).

## Author gate status

The guarded source at cfc281268 passed the complete reached heavy gate, 247/247 steps in 58.1 minutes on macOS arm64. It includes the separate default-machine correction merged upstream in #3092. The mixed-condition regression passed in the 19-test Agie writer module. Both input orders received the exact error and no files.

On the corrected production source 766fc7109, the regular CLI exported all 20 synthetic jobs. Their 32 works and 72 native files matched the previous guarded outputs byte for byte. All 20 controller-review receipts matched. All 20 repeat attempts refused to replace an existing job and preserved every byte. This corpus is a software comparison. The real control checks below cover the stated representative jobs.

The full quick gate on 766fc7109 found the missing dedicated test suite for the built-in Agie CPS dispatcher. The next commit added the suite and its 11 expected refusal records. Passing each record requires the direct single-file post to fail with the native-job diagnostic and leave no NC file.

The final head is 814dca499. It changes only tests above cfc281268. On a real plasma stream and 1300PL machine, the Agie single-file dispatcher must fail with its specific native-directory diagnostic. The workspace must exclude the post from the plasma registry. The single-file smoothing test now uses the workspace's native-post predicate. With smoothing enabled, a mounted Agie punch must refuse the setup and create no job directory. The other posts retain their previous checks.

All 49 targeted tests passed on the final head: seven plasma, seven smoothing, 12 native app, 11 native dispatcher and 12 recorded-stream tests.

The original full quick on cfc281268 ran 1,013 steps in 80.6 minutes. All but the two cross-post tests passed, including strict Clippy. On 814dca499 the official failed-step replay selected both suites and passed both in 0.8 minutes. Each suite ran seven tests. The complete 247-step heavy result belongs to cfc281268. The whole quick and heavy gates have not been repeated on 814dca499.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6 --failed gate-logs/quick-20261121-023002
```

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Integration order

The maintainer requests a separate P1 change from main and a safety-tier review of each feature PR. The standalone zero-step encoder is #3104. The first workspace writer in #2951 uses it. Keep earlier feature drafts that still generate erosion steps on hold until each takes its own safety correction and review. The standalone machine template in #2948 has no writer.

## Gate commands and pinning tests

The earlier macOS bore fixture and missing operation name were reproduced on ba5ff0ae1 with these commands:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 1d81b609c --only 'app suites: default_machine_missing'
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 1d81b609c --only 'app heavy: pocket3d_hsm'
```

The scoped CLI and native writer checks include:

- `native_punch_links_its_three_files_and_uses_the_uncompensated_contour`
- `every_punch_has_its_own_geometry_and_uses_the_requested_piece_quality`
- `nine_model_owners_resolve_all_resources_and_the_same_registered_quality`
- `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero`
- `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality`

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. Later changes clarify the repeat-import result and pin the refusal for mixed wire conditions.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. Both screenshots show the same synthetic cutoff job, DEMO2999, after the desktop Post command. The new receipt lists the control checks and the offsets of 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.

**Before · `feb802a77`**

![Earlier Post receipt reporting three files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-before.png)

**After · `814dca499`**

![Current Post receipt reporting zero working steps and the required control checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-after.png)

Effort: high
Changelog: Agie native jobs import with zero machining steps. Review each work's effective native quality and offsets before assigning its technology in Agie Control.

Fixes #2984

title: feat(wire): group independently captured punches in one native job
body:
Stacked on #2972. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/f99a9d736...issue/2961-agie-multiple-works).

## What changed

This PR posts two independently captured punches on one 20 mm plate as one native wire EDM job. It is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and onto the #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969 and #2972 ports. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Piece writer (post).** `agie_setup/piece.rs` now takes one `Piece` (stem, stock, height) and a list of `Work` (ISO stem, side, start point, exit point). It writes one quality `CCB030`, one group and the works `CUT1..n` in a loop. Each work refers to the same quality object (`ID_QUALITY,je_q1`) and has its own `ID_GEOMETRY`, `stp1` and `ASDELETE` call. The single-work SBL is byte-identical to before.
- **Group setup (post).** The new `agie_setup::PunchGroup20` takes the group stem, the stock, the 20 mm height and two `GroupPunch` entries (ISO stem and start hole). It refuses another number of works, a repeated or invalid ISO stem, a height other than 20 mm, stock outside the 350 × 250 mm span and a hole that is not completely inside the stock. The SBR has one resource line for each ISO.
- **Group export (post).** `agie::export_group_with_review` sends one job to `export_with_review` unchanged. Two jobs must be closed punches on the same 20 mm stock with a separation of 1.0 mm, and the job name has at most seven characters. Each work passes the full single-punch checks. The two cutting areas must have a clear band along X or Y. Each area includes the solid, the hole, the 3 mm lead, the longest rough miter (at least the rough offset of the thickness) and the 0.125 mm wire radius. The job has `<name>1.ISO`, `<name>2.ISO`, one SBR and one SBL, published in one directory rename.
- **App.** The post takes one or two active Wire Contour operations. Two operations must use the same setup and wire tool. Each must select a different complete modeled punch, and no other model can be present (`posting_agie_group.rs`). `agie_job` now receives its source model from the caller.
- **Docs and example.** New user-guide section "Group two captured punches", the example `examples/agie/punch-pair.camscript` (two models, `PAIR20`) and the decision file `docs/decisions/2961-agie-punch-group.md`.

## Setup fields and their sources

- All work fields are those of the control-checked zero-step punch of #2984 (golden `CCSEP20.SBL`). Only the work name, `ID_GEOMETRY` and the `stp1` position change for each work.
- The quality is created one time for the piece, as in #2984. The old branch created `QN2` and `QN3`, one name for each work. #2984 found that the control can bind different quality names to different resident data.
- One ISO for each work, the geometry, the stock (80 × 60 × 20 mm) and the holes (X-30 Y0 and X1 Y0) are those of this PR's original control-checked pair.

## Readings

- `PAIR20` from `camcraft-cli script examples/agie/punch-pair.camscript`: four files. The SBL is byte-identical to the new golden `PAIR20.SBL`.
- Emulated Agie Classic Cut 2S (offline clone of the practice control, deleted after the run):
  - The ISO and SBL bytes on the control disk match the export.
  - After import: `CUT1 CCB030[0] stp1 PAIR201.ISO` and `CUT2 CCB030[0] stp1 PAIR202.ISO`. FORMALCHECK gives one "Technologie : te definiëren" error for each work.
  - Each work shows CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0 and Te 1.5 and both options off. The CUT2 start point is X1.000 Y0.000, diameter 2.0.
  - TECCUT gives the row `0199` (Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30) and the technology `estbca25nnn060b030020` on both works. The offsets are 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm on each work. The tree then shows `CCB030[4]` on each work.
  - FORMALCHECK after TECCUT: "Controleresultaat: geen fouten" for the piece and for each work. Warnings: "Uitgekozen opties : 131072" and "Referentiewaarden : te definiëren" on each work, and "Bewerkingen : te definiëren" on the piece. A single-work job of the same frame (`SOLO20`) gives the same piece warnings.
  - GRAFICHECK: 16 cut blocks. The control cuts the four profile passes of CUT1, then of CUT2, then the four separation passes of CUT1, then of CUT2. Each separation is 1.000 mm. The moves between the works are only transit blocks (`TRA`, G00 with the head up). The cutting envelopes are CUT1 X-30.000..-9.755 Y-8.245..8.245 and CUT2 X1.000..24.245 Y-7.245..9.245. They do not touch.
- No physical cut was made.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `agie_group_setup`: `group_files_match_the_zero_step_punch_pair` (golden `PAIR20.SBL` and `PAIR20.SBR`), `each_work_has_its_own_geometry_side_and_hole`, `each_work_of_a_group_has_the_records_of_a_single_punch`, `a_group_refuses_its_unqualified_inputs`.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::group_tests`: `a_punch_pair_writes_an_iso_a_resource_line_a_work_and_a_hole_for_each_punch`, `a_single_work_through_the_group_export_keeps_its_bytes` (equal to `CCSEP20.SBL`), `a_group_rejects_an_unqualified_height_or_reserved_geometry_alias`, `a_group_refuses_a_die_three_works_another_stock_or_no_separation`, `the_band_between_punches_includes_the_rough_corner_lead_and_wire`.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native`: `group::the_two_model_owners_have_distinct_programs_holes_and_captures`, `group::a_shared_source_an_unowned_model_or_a_crossing_thread_path_writes_nothing`.
- The CCSEP20, DIE20, LOWER20 and inspection goldens and all existing tests of #2984, #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969, #2972 and #3219 are unchanged.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on `04cec49fe` (the code is the same as `912b0206f`): 523 steps, 522 pass. The one red step is `rotary_verify` `a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius`. It is red on main too (#3774) and this PR does not touch it. All `agie*` suites, `example_catalog*` and the `post`, `app` and `ui` lib tests pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No heavy step: this PR is not `P1`.

## Not exercised

- No physical cut.
- Groups of more than two works, a die or an open cutoff in a group, and heights other than 20 mm are refused. No control run covers them.
- The band check can refuse some safe nested or diagonal layouts.
- The GUI was not run. The post is the same as the CLI post.

Changelog: The native wire EDM job files post groups two independently captured punches on one 20 mm plate in one job, after it checks that their complete cutting areas stay apart.

Fixes #2961

title: feat(wire): post a straight open cutoff with separate air endpoints
body:
Stacked on #2969. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/d3443eddc...issue/2962-agie-straight-cutoff).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR adds one straight open cutoff to the native wire EDM job files post. It is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and onto the #2955, #2964, #2968 and #2969 ports. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Selection (app).** A Wire Contour with `side: left` or `side: right` takes one selected straight wall edge of the full-height retained prism. The edge must cross between opposite stock faces. The whole model must be on the side away from the kerf, inside the stock. The operation must state `both_pieces_restrained` and `stock_centered_in_xy_travel`, have no `start`, and have a run-out `clearance` of 3.6 mm or less (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`). A closed cycle still needs `capture` and a start hole.
- **New operation fields.** `both_pieces_restrained` and `stock_centered_in_xy_travel` are on `WireContourOp`, the project file (default false, so old files load unchanged), the Passes page and the MCP field list. Every other constructor, including the sketch-chain die of main, states them as false.
- **Open-cut setup (post).** The new `agie_setup::CutoffSetup20` writes the zero-step setup (ASDELETE only, no ASAGIE) with `ID_PUNCH,c_left` or `c_right`, `ID_SEPCUT,"0.0"`, `ID_EXITMODE,c_entper`, the entry point `stp1` (`ID_STPENTRY`/`ID_STPOPEN`) and the exit point `stp2` (`ID_STPEXIT`/`ID_STPOPEX`). All other fields are those of the checked zero-step punch. It refuses any thickness other than 20 mm and endpoints that are not in air beyond opposite stock faces. The SBL writer moved into `crates/post/src/agie_setup/piece.rs`; the closed and open works share it. The inspection writer of #3219 keeps its own piece script and takes `attribute_call` and `checked` from `piece.rs`; its output does not change. The CCSEP20 and DIE20 goldens do not change.
- **Routing and separation (post).** `export_with_review` sends a left or right job to `cutoff::prepare`, which returns the ISO line and the setup. The separation rule is: 0.0 for an open cut, 1.0 for a closed cycle. A closed cycle with 0.0 is still refused.
- **Geometry (post).** The ISO is the nominal line, extended 4 mm into air at each end. The entry and exit points are 3 mm to the waste side of the tail ends. The post checks the stock corners and the centered 350 × 250 mm travel with the 20 mm rough offset plus the wire radius.
- **Text.** The refusals, the CPS description, the user guide and the `camcraft-mcp` skill row name the open cutoff, beside the reentrant and die text. The guide uses the 20 mm offset row for a cutoff. No new user-facing text uses the vendor name as a feature or post name (#3537).
- **Examples.** `examples/agie/cutoff-lower.camscript` (`LOWER20`, left) and `examples/agie/cutoff-upper.camscript` (`UPPER20`, right) on original 80 × 60 × 20 mm stock.

## Readings

Offline control import on 2026-11-24 (throwaway clone of `practice-color-ready`; the base image SHA-256 did not change). Evidence (screenshots, J00 plots and the imported CamCraft files) is in the maintainer's notes folder `agie-imports-20261123/LOWER20/` and `UPPER20/`. The head of this PR posts the same bytes.

- Import: ISO and SBL bytes on the control match the CamCraft files. The new piece shows `CUT1 - CCB030[0], stp1+stp2`.
- Work details: "open contour", side Links (LOWER20) or Rechts (UPPER20), Afkortsnede 0.0, Uitlooppunt on. Inloop `stp1` and Uitloop `stp2`. `stp1` is at X−44 Y−3 (LOWER20).
- FORMALCHECK before TECCUT: one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- TECCUT header: Dia 0.25, H 20, Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0, Te 1.5. After the assignment: `CCB030[4], stp1+stp2`, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.
- FORMALCHECK after TECCUT: `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. With warnings: `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.
- GRAFICHECK (J00): four passes, each one crossing of the 88 mm line, in alternate directions. LOWER20 at Y −5.755, −5.845, −5.860 and −5.866. UPPER20 at Y 5.755, 5.845, 5.860 and 5.866. Each pass starts and ends at X±44 Y∓3 in air. These are the values of the earlier control run of this PR. The `PKT` marker 3 mm after the entry is the technology change point, as in the accepted DIE20 plot.
- Note: when the operator opens `stp2` on the Startpunt page and confirms with OK, the control can store `stp2+stp2`. A run that did not open that page kept `stp1+stp2`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `agie_cutoff_setup`: `cutoff_setup_matches_the_control_checked_zero_step_open_cut` (golden `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/LOWER20.SBL`), `right_is_the_left_setup_with_the_other_side`, `the_open_cut_shares_the_closed_setup_but_for_its_endpoints`, `endpoints_in_stock_on_one_side_or_out_of_travel_write_no_setup`.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::cutoff_tests`: `the_open_cut_includes_air_tails_wire_and_work_origin_in_travel`, `left_and_right_put_the_approach_on_the_waste_side_of_the_directed_line`, `an_open_cut_posts_zero_steps_and_no_separation_and_a_closed_cut_keeps_one_millimetre`.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` (`cutoff` module, the ported PR tests): `a_native_cutoff_has_one_nominal_crossing_and_distinct_air_endpoints` (compares the CLI SBL with the `LOWER20.SBL` golden), `unsafe_or_unconfirmed_cutoffs_publish_no_files`.
- `camcraft-app` lib `wire_edm_dto`: `cutoff_setup_statements_round_trip_and_old_files_have_neither`. `mcp_wire_contour`: `list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law`.
- `camcraft-ui` `wire_page_tests`: `the_open_cutoff_declarations_apply_and_undo_together`.
- All #2984, #2955, #2964, #2968 and #2969 tests stay green without changes to their assertions.

## Gate (head `f99a9d736`)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1190 steps, 1189 ok, 0 stalled. The one red step is `rotary_verify` `a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius`. It is red on main since #3774 and is not in this diff.
- The clippy step of the gate (`-D warnings`, with `camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-gpu`): clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`: clean.
- The merge of the new #2969 head (`d3443eddc`, with #3219) does not change the CCSEP20, DIE20 or LOWER20 goldens. The CLI output of both examples is byte-identical to the files of the control import below.

## Not exercised

- No physical cut was made.
- Only straight X- or Y-parallel cuts in 20 mm stock are accepted. Other thicknesses, oblique lines, open polygons, a drilled entry and larger clearances are refused. They have no control data.
- Heavy lanes were not run (P6).

Effort: high
Changelog: The native wire EDM job files post accepts one straight open cutoff in 20 mm stock. It writes the zero-step setup with the left or right side, separate entry and exit points in air and no separation. It requires confirmation that both pieces stay clamped and that the stock is centered in the XY travel.

Fixes #2962

title: feat(wire): post a selected convex through die opening as native wire EDM job files
body:
Stacked on #2968. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1962fd5dc...issue/2957-agie-die-opening).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR adds a die opening to the native wire EDM job files post. It is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984, the measured heights of #2964 and the reentrant checks of #2968. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Selection (app).** A Wire Contour with `side: die` takes the edge chains of the upper rim of one through-opening in one retained plate. CamCraft compares the picked rim with the full-height opening of the closed vertical prism. An outer rim, an incomplete rim and a blind floor are refused (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`).
- **Die setup (post).** `PunchSetup20::encode_die` writes the zero-step setup of `encode` with one changed field: `ID_PUNCH,c_die`. It refuses every thickness other than 20 mm (`SetupError::UnqualifiedDieHeight`). The controller review adds a check of the c_die side, the inward offsets and the slug support. The punch output does not change.
- **Mirrored geometry (post).** A die opening must be convex. The post reverses it to clockwise, so the retained plate is on the left and the waste on the right, as for a punch. The envelope check (renamed `check_cut_envelope`) then offsets toward the waste inside the opening. Its `cross < 0` test marks each opening corner as an inside corner of the plate. The reach check and `check_feature_spacing` use the rough offset of the selected thickness. The ISO object is reversed again after the seam, so the control reads a counter-clockwise opening that starts at the entry point.
- **Mirrored entry (post).** The entry code moves to `crates/post/src/agie/contour/entry.rs`. For a die, the complete 2 mm hole must lie inside each wall. The chosen wall needs 3 mm of lead and 3 mm of straight wall on each side of the foot. The foot must clear each other wall by the swept margin (0.4 mm at 20 mm). A punch keeps the supporting exterior face rule.
- **Text.** The refusals, the CPS description, the user guide and the `camcraft-mcp` skill row name the die opening. No new user-facing text uses the vendor name as a feature or post name (#3537).
- **Example.** `examples/agie/die-plate.camscript` posts the `DIE20` job from an original 60 × 60 × 20 mm plate with a 38-sided opening.

## Readings

- Earlier offline control run (comment of 2026-11-20, old writer): Agie Control plotted all 38 faces at the inward offsets 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. It cut the main profile and a 1.000 mm rough separation at X−12.255, then made three full trims. The threading point stayed at X−5.5 Y0. FORMALCHECK reported zero job errors. These offsets are the 20 mm row of `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`.
- This port (CLI, `die-plate.camscript`): 41 moves, no warning, 760.19 mm² of captured waste. `DIE20.ISO` starts at `G00 X-12.50000 Y0.00000`, then `G01 X-12.50000 Y-6.00000` (counter-clockwise). `DIE20.SBL` is byte-identical to the control-checked `CCSEP20.SBL`, except the stem, the stock (70 × 70 mm at X−35 Y−35), the start hole (X−5.5 Y0) and `ID_PUNCH,c_die`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup`: `die_setup_is_the_zero_step_punch_setup_with_the_die_side` (golden `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/DIE20.SBL`), `die_setup_is_refused_on_every_thickness_but_20_mm`.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::die_tests`: `a_die_enters_the_nearest_wall_from_inside_and_keeps_counter_clockwise_iso`, `a_die_hole_too_close_to_one_wall_enters_the_opposite_wall`, `a_die_hole_must_lie_completely_inside_the_opening`, `the_same_ring_with_an_inside_hole_is_refused_as_a_punch`, `the_reach_check_flips_every_opening_corner_to_an_inside_corner`, `a_reentrant_die_opening_is_refused`, `a_die_needs_the_rough_pass_and_wire_margin_to_the_stock`, `a_die_requires_the_qualified_20_mm_plate`, `a_die_publishes_the_zero_step_setup_with_the_die_side`.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` (`die` module, the ported PR tests): `the_selected_die_rim_posts_nominal_walls_and_inward_compensation` (compares the CLI SBL with the `DIE20.SBL` golden), `an_outer_rim_an_external_pierce_or_an_incomplete_rim_cannot_publish_a_die`, `a_blind_floor_under_the_selected_upper_rim_cannot_publish_a_die`.
- All #2955, #2964 and #2968 tests stay green without changes to their assertions.

## Gate (head `d3443eddc`)

Head `d3443eddc` merges the #2968 head `6443d4f09` into `30e6c4c3f`. That head contains `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219). No rebase and no force-push.

Conflicts and resolution:
- `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`: no conflict in this merge. The #2964 merge already resolved it: the `inspection` and `publish` modules of `main` come first, then `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`. `encode_die` and `ID_PUNCH,c_die` stay unchanged.
- `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, the Wire Contour row: the die text of this PR and the reentrant text of #2968 are both kept.
- `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`, steps 3 and 4 of the control check: step 3 uses the row of the selected stock thickness (from #2964) and says that a die plate uses the 20 mm row. Step 4 keeps the die text of this PR. Step 1 says that a die is 20 mm only. The die corner text names the 20 mm row for the 0.245 mm offset.

Results:

title: feat(wire): support checked reentrant punch contours in native wire EDM jobs
body:
Stacked on #2964. Review the reentrant punch changes above the parent head `4a94c23ce`.

## What changed

This PR replaces the convex-only refusal of #2955 with checked reentrant corners. The work is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and the measured stock heights of #2964. The old setup writer of this branch is not used.

- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/prism.rs`: `closed_vertical_prism` returns the footprint of a full-height vertical extrusion. The union of the top cap triangles must equal the union of the bottom cap triangles. The cap triangles must not overlap. Each side facet must lie on an oriented boundary face. The mesh must be one closed solid. The function examines each facet, also internal surfaces that slices do not find.
- `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`: the job takes its contour from the verified cap footprint, not from a union of slices. A union of slices can add rounded vertices along a sloping face.
- `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`: a reentrant corner is permitted when the rough offset of the selected stock thickness reaches the nominal vertex within 0.002 mm. The offset comes from `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`.
- `crates/post/src/agie/spacing.rs` (new): when the contour has a reentrant corner, each profile segment must hold both corner joins. Each pair of nonadjacent segments must keep the swept rough pass apart. The check uses the longest miter plus a full rough offset.
- The entry stays on a supporting exterior face. The ISO object keeps the nominal vertices. The SBL is the zero-step setup of main, with `ID_PUNCH c_punch` and the 1.0 mm separation.
- Refusal texts name the native wire EDM job (#3537).
- `examples/agie/notched-punch.*`: an original 40 × 20 mm punch with a 20 mm wide, 1 mm deep V notch.
- User guide and `docs/decisions/2956-agie-reentrant-punch.md`.
- `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the Wire Contour row states the checked reentrant support and its limits: the reach check with the rough offset of the selected thickness, the joins on each segment, the spacing of nonadjacent faces and the exterior entry. A notch that fails a check is refused.

## Readings

These readings are from the offline control on the old branch head `6201b325c`, before the port. That head wrote erosion steps in its own SBL.

- The control plotted all seven faces of the notched punch through the rough cut and three trims.
- Measured wire offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm.
- At X0, the four notch tips were at Y 9.246222, 9.155773, 9.140698 and 9.134668 mm. Each value agrees with the nominal slopes and the wire offset.
- The plot kept the 1 mm separation and returned to the threading hole.
- The formal check of the control had zero job errors.

### Control check of the ported writer

The offline control import of `NOTCH20`, `NOTCH40` and `NOTCH80` from the ported writer ran on 2026-11-23: see [the control import comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2968#issuecomment-7115465122). Each work showed `CCB030[0]` after import. After TECCUT, the pass offsets agreed with the row of the selected thickness, and FORMALCHECK reported no errors. The jobs came from stack head `30e6c4c3f`, which contains `1962fd5dc`. The later merges do not change a posted byte.

After the port, the notched job has the same SBL as the rectangular `CCSEP20` golden job on the same stock and start hole. Only the ISO object changes.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::reentrant_tests`:
  - `a_broad_notch_keeps_its_nominal_corner_and_requires_an_exterior_entry`
  - `a_gentle_but_narrow_notch_cannot_hold_the_rough_corner_joins`
  - `reentrant_corner_reach_uses_the_rough_offset_of_the_selected_thickness` (a 1.251 mm notch passes at 15 and 20 mm and is refused at 40 and 80 mm)
  - `the_rough_offset_is_the_largest_resident_offset_at_every_measured_height`
  - `notched_punch_posts_the_zero_step_setup_and_its_nominal_notch`
- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::tests::an_acute_miter_needs_more_stock_than_a_round_corner` (a reentrant notch that opens at 53 degrees is refused)
- `camcraft-geometry` lib, `geometry::prism::tests` (a cavity, a missing facet and a through opening)
- `camcraft-app` test `agie_native`, `reentrant::cli_posts_the_notched_punch_from_its_original_mesh` (CLI run, zero working steps, SBL equal to the `CCSEP20` golden file)

## Gate

Head `6443d4f09`. It merges the #2964 head `3a29a5f9d` (with `main` at `44e6a8269`, #3219, and the TECCUT guide fix) into `1962fd5dc`, with no conflict. Then one commit changes the Wire Contour row of `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`.

  - Green: `clippy -D warnings`, `post suites: agie_inspection`, `agie_safe_setup`, `script_agie_native`, `app suites: agie_native` (13 passed), `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.

title: feat(post): support measured Agie QN2 stock heights
body:
Stacked on #2955. Review the [height changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/9787bf79e...4a94c23ce).

The native wire EDM job files post accepts a QN2 stock thickness of 15, 20, 40 or 80 mm. Before this change, it accepted only 20 mm. Each thickness has its own measured rough offset. The corner and face clearance checks use the offset of the selected thickness. Other thicknesses are refused.

| Stock thickness (mm) | Rough (mm) | Trim 1 (mm) | Trim 2 (mm) | Trim 3 (mm) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 15 | 0.245 | 0.155 | 0.140 | 0.134 |
| 20 | 0.245 | 0.155 | 0.140 | 0.134 |
| 40 | 0.260 | 0.170 | 0.140 | 0.130 |
| 80 | 0.266 | 0.176 | 0.143 | 0.133 |

## Port onto the ported #2955 (2026-11-23)

This branch now merges the ported #2955 (`9787bf79e`), which contains `main` with #2984 and #3537. No rebase and no force-push.

Conflicts: `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`, `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`. The files of the ported #2955 are the frame. The old `jescript.rs` writer of this branch is not used.

What the port did:
- The measured table moves into `camcraft_post::agie_setup` as `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`, next to the zero-step setup that writes the height.
- `PunchSetup20` gets a `height_um` field. `encode()` refuses a thickness that is not in the table (`SetupError::UnqualifiedHeight`).
- The SBL writes the height into `ID_HEIGHT` of the piece and of the work, and `-height` into `ID_POSPOSZ`. All other SBL lines stay the same.
- The operator review text names the thickness and the four offsets of that thickness. It is now a `String`.
- `prepare()` refuses an unmeasured thickness first, with the list of supported thicknesses. `check_punch_envelope` uses the measured rough offset of the thickness for the miter. The straight face margin is the rough offset plus the 0.125 mm wire radius, rounded up to 0.1 mm. That gives 0.4 mm for all four thicknesses.
- The app-side 20 mm check is removed. The post check is the single source.
- All #2984 and #2955 checks stay: zero steps, stock and start hole, separation 1.0 mm, convex envelope, oblique entry, corner clearance.
- A 20 mm job is byte for byte the same as before: the ISO, the SBR, the SBL golden `CCSEP20.SBL`, and the review text.
- Refusal texts do not name the machine (#3537).
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row names the four thicknesses.

Process change: yes

## Pinning tests
- `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup`:
  - `each_measured_qn2_height_sets_piece_work_and_review_offsets`: the height fields and the review offsets for each thickness. Only three SBL lines change against 20 mm.
  - `an_unmeasured_qn2_height_writes_no_setup`: the refusal for 0, -20, 12, 19.999, 20.001, 25, 39.999, 60 and 100 mm.
  - `setup_files_match_the_control_checked_zero_step_punch`: the 20 mm golden and the full 20 mm review text.
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::tests`:
  - `acute_corner_clearance_uses_the_largest_resident_offset_at_the_selected_height` (from this PR).
  - `only_a_measured_qn2_thickness_prepares_a_punch`: the refusal and its text.
  - `a_measured_height_changes_only_the_setup_height_fields`: the full export at 15, 40 and 80 mm. The ISO and SBR are the same as at 20 mm.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native`: `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero` and `an_incompatible_plate_or_datum_writes_no_agie_job` (from this PR).

## Readings
Head `3a29a5f9d` merges `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219, zero-step inspection export) into `92ca17909`. No rebase and no force-push.

Conflict: `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`, one hunk at the top of the module. Main added `mod inspection; mod publish;` and the `pub use inspection::...` line. This branch added `QN2_OFFSETS_UM` and `qn2_offsets_um` at the same place. The resolution keeps the two sides: first the module lines of main, then the table. No other line changed (`git show --remerge-diff 3a29a5f9d`). The inspection export writes its own piece with a fixed 10 mm height and does not use `PunchSetup20`, so the two features do not interact.

`cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 2964 --reviewed 4a94c23ce`: NEW CODE, the one documentation commit `92ca17909` (the TECCUT step points to the row of the selected thickness). The merge commit has the one hand-resolved hunk above.

Gates on `3a29a5f9d`:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 346 steps, 2 failed, 0 stalled. Neither failure is in code of this PR:
  - `app suites: rotary_verify`, `a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius` (2110 against 2064). This is the known red of `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3774, follow-up #3794).

- By name: `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup` 6 passed, `agie_inspection` 2 passed, `script_agie_native` 11 passed; `camcraft-app` `agie_native` 12 passed.

title: feat(wire): post convex punches with oblique faces as native job files
body:
The native wire EDM job files post accepts a convex prismatic punch with straight oblique faces. Before this change, it accepted only an axis-aligned rectangular punch.

## Port onto main (2026-11-23)

This branch is now merged with `main` (#2984 and #3537 included). The port keeps the writer and the setup of `main` as the frame. It adds the checks of this PR into that frame.

What stays from `main`, unchanged:
- `prepare()` builds the guarded zero-step `PunchSetup20` first. The stock span, the 20 mm stock, the micrometre start hole and the hole-in-stock checks run before the contour checks.
- `export_with_review` refuses a separation length that is not 1.0 mm.
- The ISO, SBR and SBL files go through `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`. The old `jescript.rs` writer of this branch is not used.
- The rectangular output is byte for byte the same. The tests of `main` for the rectangle pass without a change.

What this PR adds to `main`:
- `check_punch_envelope` replaces the rectangle refusal. It refuses a reentrant corner. It checks the 0.4 mm stock margin at each vertex. It checks the miter point of the 0.245 mm rough offset and the wire allowance at each corner.
- `entry_face` and `outside_seam` replace the old entry search. The entry can be on an oblique face. The 3 mm lead and the 3 mm face length on each side are measured along the face, in exact integer arithmetic. When the perpendicular foot falls between 0.00001 mm grid points, the post selects an exterior grid point within 0.00001 mm. It then checks the envelope again on the emitted lines.
- Refusal texts name the problem, not the machine (#3537).
- The examples `examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript` and `slope-punch.camscript` use the post name "Native wire EDM job files".
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row says "a convex straight-sided punch" in place of "rectangular punch".

Process change: yes

## Pinning tests (`camcraft-post` lib, `agie::tests`)
- `oblique_punch_preserves_nominal_vertices_and_perpendicular_seam`: the nominal path of the 3:4 pentagon, both windings, and the 3 mm face-length limit.
- `oblique_punch_posts_the_zero_step_setup_and_its_faces`: the full ISO file of the oblique punch through `export_with_review`, the SBL fields of the zero-step setup, and the refusal of separation 0.0 with no output directory.
- `oblique_seam_rounds_to_the_exterior_without_moving_nominal_vertices`: the exterior grid seam.
- `outward_rounding_cannot_consume_the_required_lead_clearance`: the grid refusal.
- `an_acute_miter_needs_more_stock_than_a_round_corner`: the corner-clearance refusal and the convex refusal.
- `every_face_keeps_the_straight_stock_margin`: the 0.4 mm face margin of `main` stays.
- `separation_needs_three_millimetres_on_each_side_of_the_entry`: the entry face-length refusal of `main`.

## Readings
Head `9787bf79e`. It merges cleanly with `main` at `09ad779ee`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 11 steps, 0 failed. `camcraft-post` lib: 103 passed. Nine `camcraft-app` suites (the example catalog and first-part suites): 69 passed, 4 ignored (heavy).
- By name: `agie_native` 11 passed, `mcp_wire_contour` 8 passed, `mcp_doc_drift` 6 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- CLI: `examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript` wrote `POLY20` (entry X-12.50000 Y0.00000, all five nominal vertices). `slope-punch.camscript` wrote `SLOPE20` (exterior entry X-12.64765 Y0.50336). The receipt of each says `"working_steps_generated": false`.
- Heavy lanes: `gate heavy --dry-run` reaches 61 `camcraft-app` heavy steps through the `post` dependency. This is a `P6` PR, so no heavy step is required ("Heavy lanes at review"). None ran.
- Light lane: `gate light --dry-run` plans 4 steps (`motion` lib, `adaptive_troch_parallel`, `app` `pocket_pass_start`). None of them is in the changed code. They did not run, because the local disks had no space for a release build. The review must run them.

## Control check and not exercised
- Offline control import of the ported writer on 2026-11-23: see [the result comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2955#issuecomment-7115464026). POLY20 and SLOPE20 showed zero erosion steps after import, the matching TECCUT row, the punch side, the oblique entry and the 1.000 mm separation. FORMALCHECK gave no errors after TECCUT.
- No physical cut.

Effort: high
